THE BLOCKER, re-measured against the source rather than relayed. W3 and W5 disagree about what "belongs to a step" means. W3's join PREFERS THE STRUCTURED `step` id a round record carries (`round_step_slug`, `src/workflow.rs:119`), while W5's increment-ownership check is PURELY LEXICAL, `leading_slug(increment) != waiver.step` at `src/workflow.rs:564`, and `leading_slug` (`src/workflow.rs:88`) strips only a `-inc<alnum>` suffix. So a round record whose `task` ends in anything other than `-inc<alnum>` JOINS a step under W3 and CANNOT BE OWNED BY ANY WAIVER UNDER W5. THE AFFECTED POPULATION IS A PROPERTY, NOT A LIST, and NO COUNT OF IT IS STATED HERE, because it grows with the plan: it is every increment identity whose `leading_slug` is not the step it joins under W3, which is every identity no `[[step.waiver]]` can name without W5 refusing it. Reproduce the current set with `jq -r 'select(.type=="round") | [(.step // (.task|sub("-inc[a-zA-Z0-9]+$";""))), (.increment // .task)] | join(" ")' docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl | sort -u | awk '{lead=$2; sub(/-inc[a-zA-Z0-9]+$/,"",lead); if (lead != $1) print $1, $2}'`. TWO MEMBERS OF THAT POPULATION BLOCK A STEP TODAY and are why this item exists: `workflow-enforcement-tier-fold` and `workflow-enforcement-tier-endproperty-fold`, both plan-review loops that closed under human escalation and were never declared. THE POPULATION IS NOT CONFINED TO UNDECLARED FOLD TOKENS, and this is the part a pass must not miss: it already includes ids the plan HAS declared as `[[step.increment]]` entries. The live case is `workflow-driver`, whose declared `workflow-driver-stage0a`, `-stage0b` and `-stage1` carry no `-inc<alnum>` suffix, so `leading_slug` returns each unchanged and none can ever equal the step slug; a `[[step.waiver]]` naming one of the step's own declared increments is refused by W5 while the `src/plan/source.rs` membership check stays silent, because membership holds. THAT IS WHAT KEEPING THE LEXICAL RULE WOULD COST: renaming increment ids the plan has already declared, not merely two orphan fold tokens. W3 skips every step that is not `complete` (`src/workflow.rs:445-447`), so the `workflow-driver` case is latent rather than firing, and the same skip is why the two fold shortfalls were invisible while `workflow-enforcement-tier` was `in-progress`; flipping the status is what exposed them. TWO FACTS THE CODE ITSELF STATES ABOUT THIS AXIS, RECORDED AS MEASURED INPUTS AND NOT AS A RECOMMENDATION, in the same form the item uses for its candidate directions. FIRST, THE CODE CALLS THE LEXICAL STRIP TRANSITIONAL. `leading_slug`'s doc closes at `src/workflow.rs:83-87` with "Inc 2 retires this risk for NEW data: a `round`/`escalation` record may carry a structured `step`/`increment` id, and `round_step_slug`/`escalation_step_slug` (and their increment counterparts) prefer it, so a record with the field joins without ever reaching this lexical strip. This shim remains only for pre-migration records that omit the structured id." SECOND, W5 IS ALREADY MIGRATED ON ITS OTHER AXIS. Inside the same `w5_problems`, the increment-ownership check is lexical at `:564`, while the record-backed evidence check thirty lines later is structured, comparing through `escalation_increment_id` and `escalation_step_slug` at `:594-596` under its own comment at `:590-592`: "Tie the joined escalation to the unit the waiver exempts, preferring the escalation's structured ids (Inc 2) over the `leading_slug`/`task` shim when it carries them." One function, two checks, one migrated and one not. THE LIMIT OF BOTH FACTS, STATED BECAUSE THIS ITEM STATES LIMITS: the retirement sentence is scoped to `round` and `escalation` RECORDS that carry structured ids, and `waiver.increment` is a plan-authored id rather than a `task`, which is the doc's stated subject at `:71`. So the facts bear on the axis without settling it, and nothing here rules which direction follows from them. Measured in `docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl`: each of the two tasks carries FIVE `type:"round"` records; every one of them carries the structured `step` id `workflow-enforcement-tier` and NO structured `increment` id, so each group's identity under W3 is the full `task` (`round_increment_id`, `src/workflow.rs:127`); and the peak `consecutive_clean` is 1 for the plan fold and 0 for the endproperty fold, against the 2 their `risky` class requires.  EVERY ESCAPE ROUTE WAS CHECKED AND NONE EXISTS, recorded here so the pass does not re-derive them; each was re-verified for this registration. (1) A step-unit waiver is consulted ONLY when a step has no round records at all (`src/workflow.rs:450`), and these two have five each. (2) Naming the fold token as the waiver's own `step` is not merely refused by W5's real-Roadmap-step rule (`src/workflow.rs:553`), it is NOT AUTHORABLE AT ALL in the TOML flow: a `[[step.waiver]]` inherits `step` from the `[[step]]` that contains it (`step: step.slug.clone()`, `src/workflow.rs:258`), so the field cannot be set independently. - `Q-71` (decided -> folded into `ship-v0-0-2`) what to do first now that the 2026-08-13 workflow audit has reported, given its verdict that the workflow was not degenerate but BECAME degenerate between 2026-07-19 and 07-31, and given the fact it says frames everything else: one release, `v0.0.1`, on project day 2, 937 commits ago. OPTIONS PRESENTED: (a) fix two defects, then ship `v0.0.2`; (b) fix all four defects the audit found, then ship; (c) reform the workflow first, then ship; (d) descope the shipped guidance first, then ship. DECIDED (human, 2026-08-13): (a). THE TWO ARE THE AUDIT'S `F1` AND `F4`. `F1`: `render` interpolates free-text TOML into generated Markdown unescaped, so `escape_cell` (`src/plan/render.rs:538`) is applied at one call site of four and the projection can be made to carry structure the source never declared, which the project's own Markdown validator then rejects; this breaks the projection closure Principle 8 (Structured data first, project for humans) rests on. `F4`: `src/manifest.rs:46` and `:271` document a pack `dest` as relative to the output directory and no containment check exists anywhere, so a pack writes outside `--output-dir` while the run reports it wrote inside; the minimum fix is to make the claim true or delete it. THE RELEASE SCOPE IS EXACTLY those two fixes, the README items the `Q-65` crates.io checklist requires (link to `agent-flow`, state that the `agent-scaffold` name is reclaimable), the `agent-flow` reservation on crates.io at 0.0.2, and the `agent-scaffold` 0.0.2 publish. Nothing else. REJECTED (b) because `F2`'s fix is a real design question: joining declared increments to the round log changes what passes, so it cannot ride a release. REJECTED (c) because reforming the workflow generates no external evidence, which is what Principle 6 (Ground decisions in evidence) asks for before an approach is built out further. REJECTED (d) because deciding what to delete without knowing what anyone uses is the unvalidated build-out Principle 6 exists to prevent, however strongly Principle 2 (Minimal by default) supports the eventual descope. Folded into `ship-v0-0-2`; decision receipt `type:"decision"` `q_id:"Q-71"` in `docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl`. Decision and reasoning in `ship-v0-0-2`. Receipt: `Q-71`.

THE DEFECT: an `[[asset]].source` in a `--template` pack can name a path outside the pack directory, because `PackSource::Directory::read` (`src/manifest.rs:307`) is a bare `root.join(rel)` and `src/manifest.rs:44` only documents the field as "within the pack", so `scaffold` copies an arbitrary readable file into the scaffolded project under a legal `dest`. It is the read-side twin of the `F4` write escape this step already fixes, in the same struct, and the containment predicate that closes it is created by the `F4` fix in the same change. REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY by the orchestrator and again by the planning pass at `d06f1b5`: a pack whose only asset carries `source = "../secret.md"` and `dest = "leaked.md"` exits 0, prints `create  leaked.md`, and lands the outside file's contents in the scaffolded project; an absolute `source` does the same. OPTIONS PRESENTED: (a) fix it in this step; (b) ship 0.0.2 without it and fix it in the next step; (c) ship it and document the trust boundary in the README, as `src/checks.rs:17-26` argues for `.agents/checks.toml`. DECIDED (human, 2026-08-13): (a), which was also the orchestrator's recommendation. THE REASONING THE HUMAN ACCEPTED: it is one bounded application of a predicate that already exists in this change rather than newly discovered work; enforcing containment on `dest` but not on `source` in the same struct is an incoherent boundary rather than a smaller one (Principle 5, Make illegal states unrepresentable, and Principle 1, Prefer the cleaner long-term architecture over the smallest diff); and taking it before the review round costs no extra rounds, because `ship-v0-0-2-inc1` is `low_risk` and one clean round converges it. THE REASONING AGAINST, WEIGHED AND OVERRIDDEN RATHER THAN ABSENT, RECORDED SO THE EXCEPTION STAYS VISIBLE AS ONE: the step's own sidecar states that its purpose is delivery, so its scope is closed and every addition to it defeats it; and the 2026-08-13 audit measured steps generated by the process itself at 8.3% before the 2026-07-19 to 07-31 turn and 54.2% after it, marked monotonic, so "just this once, it is small" is the exact habit that produced that number. REJECTED (c) because a `--template` pack is external input the user may have fetched from anywhere, whereas `.agents/checks.toml` is the user's own configuration in their own repository, so the trusted-config argument does not carry over; this is the argument `ship-v0-0-2` already makes against the same option for `F4`. THE SCOPE IS WIDENED ONCE AND THE CLOSED-SCOPE SENTENCE STANDS: this decision is its only exception, and a second addition needs its own human decision rather than this precedent. THE OPEN CAUSATION QUESTION, LEFT FOR LATER AND RECORDED HERE IN FULL BECAUSE THE INVESTIGATION HAS NEVER BEEN RUN AND NOBODY HAS EVER BEEN TASKED WITH IT. The 2026-08-13 audit established WHEN the loop turned and WHAT changed. It did not establish WHY, and nothing since has. Its record dates the transition to "roughly 2026-07-19 through 07-31", states that five auditors working on different questions and without coordinating independently identified the same fortnight, and puts two of its six measures at 07-19 exactly: documentation to code by bytes, 1.28:1 before and 5.17:1 after, and net Rust delivered per week, +3,733 before and +48 after.  THE UNTESTED HYPOTHESIS VISIBLE IN THE DATA is that the `structured-skeleton` plan-as-data migration created a large machine-readable plan surface, which the review loop then began reviewing. Its dates: `Q-45` and `Q-46` decided 2026-07-18, and the six increments built and closed out on 2026-07-19 (`a4d0e0c`). The data in which the hypothesis is visible is the audit's Condition 3: 31% of all findings come from reviewing PLANNING DOCUMENTS, which supply 20 of the project's 32 high-severity findings, and six consecutive late loops covering 154 findings across 22 rounds found ZERO defects in what the software does.  IT IS UNTESTED. Nothing in the audit record tests it, and no measurement anywhere in this repository does. COINCIDENCE AND REVERSE CAUSATION ARE BOTH LIVE, for two reasons. FIRST, the window is the project's largest delivery burst, so a supposed cause and its supposed effect share a stretch that is exceptional for other reasons as well: 2026-07-18 and 07-19 are the project's two highest net `src/*.rs` days, at +3,745 and +5,430 lines, and 2026-07-17 to 07-19 is +10,341 net lines against +3,297 for the three days before it (measured 2026-08-14 with `git log --numstat` over `src/*.rs`). SECOND, the audit's own measure that most directly expresses the hypothesis, steps generated by the process itself rising from 8.3% to 54.2%, is marked MONOTONIC rather than dated, so it does not turn at 07-19 and cannot be used to date a cause there. The reverse direction reads as well against the record as it stands: the loop began reviewing plan documents because delivery had stopped, rather than delivery stopping because the loop began reviewing plan documents. - `Q-77` (decided -> folded into `user-prompts-pointer-and-drift-coverage`) what to do about `audit` naming two unrelated things in one product, now that the rename has shipped and the moment to settle it with the name change has passed. THE COLLISION, measured on the tree at `cd97c7e`: `agent-flow audit` is the subcommand that writes the advisory code-value report (`src/audit.rs`, built by the `code-value-audit-static` step), and `.agents/user-prompts/audit.md` is the human-invoked prompt carrying the pre-registered measurement method (built by `audit-user-prompt`). They share no machinery, no input and no output. One reports which code may be dead; the other runs a controlled empirical study of a claim about the project. A user who reads `agent-flow --help` and then the prompt list has nothing but the word to tell them apart. RAISED BY A REVIEWER during the 0.0.3 release work and out of that review's scope, so nothing has ruled on it and no receipt exists. OPTIONS, NONE PRE-DECIDED, each carrying a cost that has to be priced rather than assumed: (a) rename the subcommand, which is a breaking CLI change in a product that has just spent one on the crate name; (b) rename the prompt, which is a pack asset rename and cheap, though `audit` is the word the method is known by and the prompt is the artifact that teaches it; (c) keep both and disambiguate in the `audit` help text and in the prompt list, which is the cheapest and leaves the collision standing; (d) rule the collision acceptable, on the ground that a subcommand and a pasted prompt are different surfaces and a user never picks between them, and record that ruling so it is not re-raised. THE TIMING FACT THAT BEARS ON IT, recorded because it is the reason this is a question rather than a task: the rename was the one moment when a name change carried no marginal cost to a user, since 0.0.3 already required every invocation to be rewritten, and that moment is gone. From here, option (a) costs a second breaking change and option (b) costs a second pack churn, so the price of (a) and (b) went up on 2026-08-15 while the price of (c) and (d) did not. Do not decide here.  DECIDED (human, 2026-08-15): (c), keep both names and disambiguate them, in the `audit` subcommand's help text and in the shipped prompt list. The "Do not decide here" instruction above bound the pass that raised the question, and this paragraph is the decision it was held for. (c) was also the orchestrator's recommendation. THE RECEIPT'S OPTION ORDER IS NOT THIS ASK'S LETTER ORDER, recorded so the two reconcile without guessing: the receipt presents `Keep both, disambiguate`, `Rule it acceptable, record it`, `Rename the prompt file` and `Rename the subcommand`, which are (c), (d), (b) and (a) here, and its `chosen` value is `Keep both, disambiguate`, so the human chose (c). THE PRINCIPLE THAT ARGUES THE OTHER WAY, STATED RATHER THAN OMITTED. Prefer the cleaner long-term architecture over the smallest diff argues for a rename: a name that denotes two unrelated things is a permanent comprehension cost, and a clause in two files documents that cost rather than removing it. It is overridden by the timing fact this ask already records, not by a claim that the collision is harmless. WHAT THAT LEAVES OPEN: this decision does not bar renaming either thing at a future breaking release, and it does not make the collision correct. It closes the question under the plan's ordinary rule, that a folded decision reopens only on evidence that beats its recorded reasoning, and a breaking release is such evidence, because the cost that decided this question is the marginal cost to a user and that cost is different when every invocation is being rewritten anyway. WHAT IS MEASURED TODAY, each fact re-derived rather than carried from the brief that raised this. The measurements are taken on the tree this item is authored into, which is `e8b2992` plus this pass's own two additions, so the step and question counts below read 101 and 78 rather than the 100 and 77 that stand at `e8b2992`.  - THE SCHEMA HAS NO PLACE FOR IT. The `Step` struct (`src/plan/source.rs:129`) carries nine keys: `slug`, `title`, `status`, `order`, `blocked_by`, `folds`, `provenance`, `increment` and `waiver`. None of them states the problem a step addresses or the approach it takes. `provenance` (`Provenance`, `src/plan/source.rs:240`) holds `decisions`, `findings` and `commits`, which is WHY THE STEP EXISTS BY REFERENCE, an adjacent thing rather than a statement of intent: it names the artifacts that justify the step and says nothing about what the step is for. - THE INTENT LIVES ONLY IN THE SIDECAR, AND ONLY ITS EXISTENCE IS CHECKED. A step's intent is prose in `docs/plans/<task>.steps/<slug>.md`, bound by filename convention at `src/plan/render.rs:180`. `render` is strict about the file BEING THERE (a missing sidecar exits non-zero and writes nothing) and inspects its CONTENT not at all: `step_details_section` (`src/plan/render.rs:573`) inlines the blob verbatim, and its own doc comment records that "each sidecar carries its own `### <slug>` heading". So the binding is checked and the text is not. - THE PACK ALREADY ASKS FOR THE INTENT AND ALREADY ENFORCES NOTHING, which sharpens the question from "should intent be recorded" to "where should it live and what should check it". The scaffolded step-sidecar template, `pack/plan-template.steps/example-step.md` and its rendered copy `docs/plans/TEMPLATE.steps/example-step.md`, is one heading plus one instruction: "What this step does and how; once done, the outcome and the evidence." That is the problem-and-approach this item is about, already written into every scaffolded project, as a placeholder note a planner deletes. So the convention exists in prose and has no representation in the schema, no check and no query. - THE SIDECAR ALREADY HAND-DUPLICATES TWO TOML FIELDS WITH NO CROSS-CHECK, which is the existing precedent any answer inherits. Because the heading is the sidecar's own, `slug` and `title` are written twice, once as TOML data and once as prose. Measured over all 101 step sidecars: 90 open with a `###` heading whose first token is the backticked slug, 5 open with a `####` heading of that same form (the sub-steps of an umbrella), 5 open with a `###` umbrella heading that names no slug (`mode-enum`, `pack-manifest`, `convergence-accounting`, `file-safety-rules`, `exploration-mode`), and `core-assets` opens with no heading at all. - NO SUBCOMMAND ANSWERS THE QUESTION. `agent-flow --help` lists seven: `scaffold`, `validate`, `status`, `next`, `checks`, `render` and `audit`. `status` prints counts and nothing else (`plan: 101 steps (68 complete, 17 deferred, 3 in progress, 6 not started, 3 optional, 4 skipped); 78 open-questions items`). `next` names one step and the role prompt to hand an agent. `render` emits the whole plan document, which is a projection rather than a query. So a human or an agent asking "what is this step for and how does it address it" opens a file.  THE COST OF THE UNCHECKED HALF IS MEASURED RATHER THAN PREDICTED, AND IT IS MORE THAN TEN TIMES THE FIGURE THIS ITEM WAS ROUTED ON. A sweep of every one of the 101 step sidecars against its step's declared `status` finds 21 whose opening status token contradicts it: 10 `complete` steps open "Not started", 7 `complete` steps open "Next", 2 `complete` steps open "Deferred", and 2 of the 3 `in-progress` steps open "Not started". The enumeration, the method, the compatible-pair exemption and the command that reproduces the list are in `sidecar-status-opening-drift`, which fixes them and is itself the 101st step. The human routed this item on 2 observed cases; the population is 21, so the pass must price its options against 21. This is the strongest evidence available on what an unvalidated sidecar convention costs over the plan's 101 steps and the 40 days from the repository's first commit (2026-07-09) to today, and it bears directly on option (a) below, because a schema field is checked by the parser and a paragraph is not.  THE TWO OPTIONS PUT TO THE HUMAN, RECORDED WITH THE COST THAT STOPPED EACH FROM BEING TAKEN ON THE SPOT, so the pass extends the space rather than rediscovering it. (a) STRUCTURED FIELDS, THEN A QUERY COMMAND: add the problem and the approach as fields on `[[step]]`, then a subcommand that projects them. This is the plan's own Principle 8 answer (Structured data first, project for humans) and may well be where the pass lands, and it was rejected AS AN IMMEDIATE COMMITMENT because it touches every step in the plan, needs a backfill, and had not been priced against the alternatives. (b) QUERY COMMAND ONLY, FIRST: a subcommand projecting the existing sidecar prose with no schema change. It is the cheapest and it ships value immediately, and it leaves the intent text unvalidated, so the drift the sweep measured stays possible. NEITHER IS PRE-DECIDED HERE and the pass may reject both.  WHAT THE PASS MUST SETTLE. None of these is pre-decided, and the list is what the pass owes back rather than a substitute for the evidence above.  - (a) THE ENCODING. Required schema fields, optional schema fields, or a validated sidecar contract (a required section, checked by `render` or by `validate --plan`). Required fields make the absence of intent unrepresentable (Make illegal states unrepresentable) and force the backfill; optional fields make partial adoption legal and make "no intent recorded" indistinguishable from "not yet backfilled" unless something else distinguishes them; a validated sidecar contract keeps the prose where it is and checks its shape, which catches an absent section and not a stale one. Say which failures each form actually catches, because the measured drift is a STALE claim rather than an ABSENT one, and a presence check catches only the second. - (b) THE BACKFILL. 101 steps, of which 68 are `complete`, 17 `deferred`, 6 `not started`, 4 `skipped`, 3 `optional` and 3 `in progress`. Decide whether a `complete` step owes intent at all, whether partial adoption is coherent, and if it is, what makes the un-backfilled steps visible rather than silently empty. The plan already has one declared-exemption pattern to weigh, `[meta].w4_baseline`, which makes the exemption boundary declared data rather than inferred, and one nested-exemption pattern in `[[step.waiver]]`. - (c) THE QUERY. A new subcommand, or a flag on `status`, or an option on `next`. Decide what it shows for one step and for many, whether it has a `--json` form like its siblings, and what it does for a step whose intent is absent. Note that `status` is documented as "Best-effort; a missing file yields a partial projection" while `render` is strict, so the two established stances differ and the query has to pick one. - (d) THE INTERACTION WITH THE THREE EXISTING READERS. `render` inlines the sidecar verbatim and would have to decide whether a structured intent field is projected into the Step Detail (a second copy of the same fact) or replaces part of it. `next` builds the brief an agent is handed, so intent is the fact most likely to belong there, and its `context` block is where it would go. `validate --plan` is the only place a content rule could be enforced without changing `render`'s contract. - (e) THE ASYMMETRY BETWEEN STEPS AND QUESTIONS, WHICH NO OPTION AS PUT ACCOUNTS FOR, AND WHICH IS MEASURED. The plan's two halves answer "where does the prose live" in OPPOSITE ways. All 78 `<task>.questions/<id>.md` sidecars are 0 bytes, and a question's whole body is the TOML `ask` string. Every one of the 101 `<task>.steps/<slug>.md` sidecars carries the body, and the TOML holds no prose for a step beyond `title`. So the project has already run both experiments, and the question half is the one with no drift class of this kind available to it, because there is no second copy to go stale. The pass must either explain why steps and questions should differ or propose unifying them, and it must not adopt an answer for steps that contradicts the shipped answer for questions without saying so. - (f) WHAT "INTENT" IS, before it is encoded. The brief that raised this names two things, the problem and the approach. A step sidecar in this repo today typically carries more: the measured evidence, the alternatives considered and rejected, the scope boundary, the cost stated so it is weighed, and the executable acceptance criteria. Decide which of those are intent, which are already covered by `provenance`, and which stay prose. Encoding two fields and leaving the rest unstructured is a legitimate answer and it needs stating rather than assuming. - (g) WHETHER A SIDECAR MAY RESTATE A TOML FIELD AT ALL, WHICH THIS PLAN HAS ALREADY ANSWERED FOR ITSELF AND NO SCAFFOLDED PROJECT INHERITS. `docs/plans/agent-scaffold.documentation-protocol.md:5` ends "The Step Details below carry each step's design, decisions, and (once done) outcome and evidence, and do not repeat the status label", and the ledger records the duplication ruled a valid defect twice, at `:62` (round 2 `G1`, `high`) and at `:101` (round 3 `L1`, left unfixed only because it is plan-wide). `Q-78-statusform` (human, 2026-08-18) acted on that for the 21 mismatching openings, which `sidecar-status-opening-drift` deletes rather than rewrites. THE PASS INHERITS TWO THINGS FROM THAT, neither pre-decided. First, 24 sidecars keep an accurate status label and are outside that step's scope, so the protocol sentence stays false at 24; decide whether they are swept, and by what. Second, `pack/plan-template.documentation-protocol.md` carries NO equivalent sentence, so the rule is local to this plan and no scaffolded project inherits it; decide whether it belongs in the pack, and whether it generalises past `status` to the `slug` and `title` the sidecar heading also duplicates. - (h) THE `next` OBSERVATION, RECORDED AS EVIDENCE AND RULED A SEPARATE DEFECT. `agent-flow next --source docs/plans/agent-scaffold.plan.toml` reports `workflow-calibration` as the active loop at `awaiting-first-review`, `rounds 0/5`, and offers a reviewer. The arithmetic is correct on its own terms: `select_active_loop` (`src/next.rs:709`) takes the lowest-order `in-progress` step and builds a review loop from it, `workflow-calibration` is order 35 against `workflow-driver` at 52 and `code-value-audit-static` at 86, and no `round` record names it. The step is in an exploration phase, not a review loop. THE VERDICT: this is a defect in `next`, not a part of this question, because it is reachable and fixable with no schema change at all, and it owes its own step and its own human decision. It is recorded here because the pass may find that a step's encoded intent or phase is the clean way to tell an exploration from a review loop, in which case the two answers interact, and because the pass should not assume `next` is a fixed constraint.  THE TWO SUB-DECISIONS THIS QUEUE HOLDS NO ENTRY OF ITS OWN FOR, so this paragraph and item (g) are the queue's only pointers to them. `Q-78-statusdrift` (human, 2026-08-18) decided to correct the stale sidecar openings NOW, as their own step, over folding them into this design pass and over flipping the affected statuses to `not-started` instead. It follows the `Q-55-<suffix>` convention of a receipt without a registered `[[question]]`, so it is cited by receipt (`type:"decision"`, `q_id:"Q-78-statusdrift"`, in `docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl`, added by commit `e8b2992`). Its step is `sidecar-status-opening-drift`, which carries the enumeration and the acceptance criteria and does NOT depend on this pass's outcome: it corrects false statements and settles no rule. `Q-78-statusform` (human, 2026-08-18) then decided that step's FORM: DELETE the token rather than replace it and record the residual, over keeping the label with the protocol sentence recorded as an exclusion, over keeping it and routing the conflict to item (g), and over cutting the step's justification prose down to what the criteria need. It follows the same convention (`type:"decision"`, `q_id:"Q-78-statusform"`, in `docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl`, added by commit `5ca89bb`), and item (g) above records what this pass inherits from it.  Do not build until decided. When the pass has run, the item moves to `open` and the options go to the human under the human-input contract. Receipt: `Q-78`.
