## The blocker, re-measured for this fold

`leading_slug` (`src/workflow.rs:88`) strips only a `-inc<alnum>` suffix. So an increment identity whose `leading_slug` is not the step it joins under W3 CANNOT BE OWNED BY ANY WAIVER UNDER W5, whatever the plan says. THE AFFECTED POPULATION IS A PROPERTY, NOT A LIST: it is every identity in that shape, and it grows with the plan. Reproduce the current set with

```
jq -r 'select(.type=="round") | [(.step // (.task|sub("-inc[a-zA-Z0-9]+$";""))), (.increment // .task)] | join(" ")' docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl | sort -u | awk '{lead=$2; sub(/-inc[a-zA-Z0-9]+$/,"",lead); if (lead != $1) print $1, $2}'
```

TWO MEMBERS BLOCK A STEP TODAY, `workflow-enforcement-tier-fold` and `workflow-enforcement-tier-endproperty-fold`, both plan-review loops that closed under human escalation and were never declared. THE REST ARE LATENT FOR THREE DIFFERENT REASONS, and the third is the one the `Q-70` item does not model. First, W3 skips every step that is not `complete` (`src/workflow.rs:445-447`), which is why the `workflow-driver` trio (`-stage0a`, `-stage0b`, `-stage1`, all DECLARED `[[step.increment]]` entries that carry no `-inc<alnum>` suffix) does not fire. Second, the same skip hid the two blockers while `workflow-enforcement-tier` was `in-progress`; flipping the status is what exposed them. THIRD, AND THIS IS THE ONE TO CARRY: a member can sit inside an ALREADY-`complete` step and stay silent because its increments CONVERGED, so no waiver was ever needed and W5 was never consulted about it. The current instance is `decision-folder-currency-fold`. FLIPPING A STEP TO `complete` IS THEREFORE NOT SUFFICIENT TO EXPOSE A MEMBER, and a reader who takes the first two reasons as exhaustive will under-estimate the population.

## The decided fix

Direction (iii), stated against the round log rather than against the plan. All three explorers reached it independently from different lenses, and each BUILT it rather than proposing it.

1. `run_checks` (`src/workflow.rs:206-221`) ALREADY HOLDS the `rounds` slice and already hands it to `w3_problems`; it simply does not hand it to `w5_problems`, which today takes `waivers`, `steps` and `escalations` (`src/workflow.rs:544-548`). Widen the signature and pass it through.
2. EXTRACT THE SHARED PREDICATE. The relation the fix needs already exists inside W3's covering-waiver match at `src/workflow.rs:498-502`, which compares the waiver's `(step, increment)` pair against the round-log grouping structurally. Extract it into one named predicate over `round_step_slug`/`round_increment_id` and have BOTH W3 and W5 consult that one implementation, so the two cannot drift apart again. This is the repository's own established idiom for this class: `peak_consecutive_clean` is `pub(crate)` precisely so `next` and W3 run identical arithmetic, and `WaiverReason::required_tier` is single-sourced between W5 and `src/plan/source.rs`.
3. REPLACE the lexical comparison at `:564` with a lookup into that predicate, so every refusal W5 emits is backed by a record rather than by a substring. The message must stop naming a step derived from the id, which is the first of the two `src/` defects above.
4. The rule text moves with the code; see Documentation impact.

WHY THE FIX SHIPS FIRST AND ALONE, which is the pass's central finding and the reason inc1 is sequenced by itself. The coupling question the pass was commissioned to answer is a CONSEQUENCE OF THE DIRECTION rather than an empirical unknown: under (iii) the W5 rule and the prospective waiver-note join resolve through the SAME round-log predicate, so they share a join; under (i) they would key on two different sets. And the recorded schema constraint binds the OTHER pair, not this one: project identity adds `project` to `Round` and the note join needs `valid_findings` on the same `Round`, so THOSE two couple, while direction (iii) ADDS NO FIELD TO ANY STRUCT. `Q-55-mechanism`'s "one deliberate edit rather than a rider on a path fix" therefore binds the note join and project identity and DOES NOT BIND THE W5 FIX.

## Declaring the two fold tokens is necessary, not merely insufficient

`Q-70`'s escape route 4 records that declaring `workflow-enforcement-tier-fold` and `workflow-enforcement-tier-endproperty-fold` as `[[step.increment]]` entries does not admit the owed waivers. That is true against the shipped binary and it is only half the fact. A SECOND VALIDATION PATH runs on the TOML substrate: the per-step waiver loop at `src/plan/source.rs:791-856` builds the step's declared increment set (`:792-793`) and checks the waived increment's membership in it (`:807-811`). That check is a HARD GATE no change to W5 can bypass, and two explorers measured it firing against a direction (iii) build with the tokens left undeclared. So DECLARING IS REQUIRED UNDER EVERY DIRECTION, and every proposal's edit surface includes a plan edit as well as a source edit.

THE ORDER MATTERS AND IS PART OF INC1. Declaring alone leaves W5 refusing; fixing alone leaves the source path refusing; the two together return `workflow invariants hold` at exit 0, which two explorers measured end to end on a fixture carrying both declarations, both owed waivers and the step flipped to `complete`. The declaration and the status flip are the orchestrator's own direct-on-main integration edits; the two waivers are plan content and are authored by the planner. Their drafted notes are already in the ledger, found by a line-start anchored grep for "TWO WAIVERS ARE OWED AND CANNOT YET BE WRITTEN", so the next agent does not have to reconstruct them. NEITHER WAIVER MAY BE WRITTEN BEFORE THE CODE LANDS: writing them first turns `validate --workflow` red, which is the state this step exists to end.

ONLY THE OWNERSHIP CHECK BLOCKS THEM, which bounds the fix. Each fold token already has a `type:"escalation"` record whose `task` equals it and whose `human_decision` is `decision`, and which carries no structured `increment` id, so W5's record-backed evidence join resolves through the `task` fallback (`escalation_increment_id`, `src/workflow.rs:141`) and passes.

## The known behaviour change, and the one point the pass left open

DIRECTION (iii) IS NOT BEHAVIOUR-NEUTRAL, and `Q-70` prices it as though it were. Under the lexical rule, an increment-unit waiver whose increment has NO round records at all passes W5 silently, because the rule only compares strings. Under the round-log rule there is nothing for it to join to, so the fix NARROWS WHAT A WAIVER MAY COVER. There is no live regression: one explorer ran its prototype against the unmodified plan and log and got `workflow invariants hold` at exit 0, so every waiver currently committed to this plan satisfies the new rule with no edit to any waiver and no edit to the append-only log. Re-establish that before relying on it, with the whole live plan as the fixture.

THE OPEN POINT, RECORDED AS OPEN BECAUSE THE PASS DID NOT SETTLE IT AND THE HUMAN HAS NOT DECIDED IT. The explorers' prototypes DIVERGED on the unobserved case. Two REPORT it, ON TWO INDEPENDENT GROUNDS, which is a stronger record than one ground credited twice, so each is attributed to the file that gives it. The architecture lens (`Q-70-architecture.md:286`) keeps the branch because it is the only thing that catches a typo'd increment id on the Markdown and JSONL substrate, where no declared set exists to catch it. The evidence lens (`Q-70-evidence.md:165`) keeps it on a different ground entirely: a waiver covering an increment with no round records grants nothing in W3 anyway, since W3's increment loop is built from the records so an increment with none never enters it, and reporting it turns a dead waiver into a visible one, which is Make illegal states unrepresentable applied to a waiver. One leaves W5 SILENT there, on the ground that the increment has nothing to attribute yet and that `src/plan/source.rs:807` already catches the undeclared case on the TOML path; that explorer measured the residual honestly, namely that an increment both DECLARED and never logged would then pass W5 silently. The implementer states which it took and argues it, or raises it as a fork. The step's default is to REPORT, because it is the substrate-uniform answer and because the narrowing is then visible rather than implicit, and it is carried with a test either way (acceptance check 4).

THIS OPEN POINT ALSO EXPLAINS A DISAGREEMENT IN THE MEASURED EDIT SURFACE, so do not treat the difference as one explorer being wrong: the number of existing W5 unit tests that need a round-log fixture rather than a mechanical empty slice IS A FUNCTION OF THIS CHOICE. Under the reporting form, every test that constructs an increment-unit waiver with no log needs a fixture; under the silent form, only the test that exercises a genuine mis-scoped waiver does.

## The increments, and why in this order

The division follows the rule this plan already uses: an increment is a unit whose review asks ONE question.

- `validation-constraints-inc1`, THE W5 OWNERSHIP FIX AND THE UNBLOCKING. The shared predicate, the widened `w5_problems`, the replaced rule body and its two fact-backed messages, the tests, the rule text in its three prose copies, and then the plan-side unblocking: the two `[[step.increment]]` declarations, the two owed waivers, and `workflow-enforcement-tier` flipped to `complete`. The review question is "does the ownership rule now assert a fact the round log records, and does the blocked step actually unblock".
- `validation-constraints-inc2`, THE SIBLING REAL-STEP RULE AT `src/workflow.rs:553`. On the TOML path a `[[step.waiver]]` inherits its `step` from the containing `[[step]]` (`step: step.slug.clone()`, `src/workflow.rs:258`) and the typed `Waiver` struct (`src/plan/source.rs:279-300`) is `deny_unknown_fields` with no `step` field at all, while `check_workflow_toml` derives both `plan.step_views()` and `waivers_from_toml(plan)` from the same `plan.steps`, so the rule cannot fire there. THE TREATMENT IS NOT PRE-DECIDED. One reading is that an unreachable rule is a success rather than a bug, the substrate having made the bad state unrepresentable, in which case the work is to say so where the rule is documented and to keep it live on the JSONL substrate, where `step` is a free string and the state IS authorable. The other is that a rule whose premise cannot hold on the project's own substrate should be restructured. The implementer takes one, argues it, or raises the fork. IT ALSO CARRIES `B5`, the unpinned evidence-pointer clause described in the members section above, whose remedy is one test on the fixture shape recorded there. The review question widens by one clause to carry it and is "is the rule's reachability now described truthfully, on both substrates, and is the evidence pointer pinned as load-bearing". That is a deliberate departure from this step's one-question division rule, taken because `B5` sits in the only other increment that touches `w5_problems` and costs one test there; declaring it separately is authorised and not taken.
- `validation-constraints-inc3`, THE `validate` UNREADABLE-INPUT DEFECT FAMILY, whose members are enumerated with their ledger anchors in the members section above and are not re-listed or counted here. They are one increment because they share one surface, `validate`'s report about an input it cannot fully resolve, and because a reviewer who has built the fixture for one has most of the fixture for the next. THE REVIEW QUESTION HAS TWO CLAUSES BECAUSE THE FAMILY HAS TWO INPUTS, and it is stated so that a reviewer has a prompt for each: "does `validate` report truthfully about an input it cannot read, on the LOG input and on the PLAN-SOURCE input alike, whichever way each is unreadable; and can the containment guard still be defeated between the check and the use". THE ALTERNATIVE DIVISION IS AUTHORISED AND NOT TAKEN, recorded so that taking it later needs no new decision: the plan review's triage ruled that if the one-question rule makes `R3A-3` a poor fit here it must be declared as its own increment rather than dropped, and the axis it named is the LOG input versus the PLAN-SOURCE input. It is kept as one increment because the two members that carry the entry gate above (`R2A-4` and `R3A-3`) sit on opposite sides of that axis and may share one treatment decision, so splitting on it would separate two defects a human may have to rule on together.
- `validation-constraints-inc4`, THE `agent-scaffold next` TRUTHFULNESS DEFECTS: the false completion recommended from a converged last increment while the sidecar commits to unbuilt work, the oversized output from dumping the ledger resume state verbatim, and the calm exit reporting "no plan source" when `--source` is omitted. One review question, "does `next` say something true and proportionate", and one surface.
- `validation-constraints-inc5`, THE UNPOPULATED `blocked_by` FIELD. UNPOPULATED, NOT UNREAD, and the distinction is the whole of this bullet's correction: the ledger records the field as empty and states its consequence in terms of what `next` ADVISES, and this file's first draft converted that into "nothing reads it" and then priced the increment on the converted claim. Only the emptiness half is true. Re-measured for this fold with line-start anchored greps, since the naive form has an exception in prose: `grep -c '^\[\[step\]\]$'` and `grep -c '^blocked_by = \[\]$'` over the plan TOML return the same number, so the field is empty on every step and populated on none. THE FIELD IS READ IN FOUR PRODUCTION SITES, each read at the line for this correction: `src/plan/render.rs:478-488`, `notes_cell`, which pushes one blocked note per blocker into the Notes cell of every Roadmap row in the generated `<task>.md`; `src/next.rs:720-732`, which selects the pending step `next` recommends by `blockers_met` and otherwise returns a `Blocked` loop; `src/next.rs:737-751`, `blockers_met` and `unmet_blockers`, with `:1012` filling the emitted instruction's `blocked_by` slot; and `src/plan/source.rs:599-608`, the cross-reference that flags a self-reference or a dangling slug. So a single blocker rewrites a Roadmap row and can flip which step `next` recommends. Split from inc4 for a reason the record itself gives: populating `blocked_by` is PLAN CONTENT and so planner work, whereas inc4 is source work, so the two are authored by different roles against different artifacts and reviewed by different questions. THE TREATMENT IS NOT PRE-DECIDED: populate it, teach `next` to honour it further, retire the field, or some pair of those, and the fork is now stated against what the field already does rather than against a false premise that it does nothing. The review question is "does the structured source now encode the ordering that today lives only in ledger prose, and does every surface that already reads the field still say something true afterwards".
- `validation-constraints-inc6`, THE ONE DELIBERATE RECORD-SCHEMA EDIT AND THE SHARED ROOT CAUSE. Project identity on `Round` and on `[meta]` with the join filtered in `check_workflow_toml`, plus `project_root_of_source`'s fallback, which the record queues as one treatment with it. Its three recorded limitations are inherited from the `workflow-enforcement-tier` explorer that built it: it is opt-in, so an unmigrated plan is unprotected; a filter placed inside `run_checks` does not cover `next`, which derives its forward verdict independently; and `decisions` and `escalations` are read unfiltered. A FOURTH LIMITATION IS ADDED HERE, and it exists only because inc1 lands first, so it could not have been recorded before this step: `check_workflow_toml` computes the rounds at ONE site (`src/workflow.rs:189`) and hands them to `run_checks` (`:206-221`), so a filter applied there is inherited by every check that reads them, and after inc1 W5 is one of those checks. THE FILTER'S PLACEMENT THEREFORE GOVERNS W5'S OWNERSHIP VERDICT AS WELL AS W3'S CONVERGENCE VERDICT, and the hazard follows from the first limitation rather than from anything new: identity is opt-in, so on a merged log this plan's own pre-migration rounds carry no `project`, and a filter keeping only rounds whose `project` matches would drop them all, at which point under inc1's DEFAULT reporting form W5 reports EVERY increment-unit waiver in the plan because no surviving round joins any waived increment. Measure the size of that blast radius rather than carrying a figure: `grep -c '^unit = "increment"$' docs/plans/agent-scaffold.plan.toml` counts the waivers it would turn red on a correct plan. AND AN ORDERING CONSTRAINT CARRIED FROM THE SAME SOURCE PARAGRAPH AS THE THREE LIMITATIONS, which this step's first draft inherited the limitations from and dropped: explorer B's negative result, recorded in `docs/plans/agent-scaffold.steps/workflow-enforcement-tier.md`, is that declaring the log's LOCATION does not establish that the log BELONGS to the plan, and that building a path field first would make the identity work harder, because the identity check would then have to reconcile itself against a declared path that may disagree with it. So no declared log-path field is built before the identity work. The review question is "does an identity that is declared actually separate two projects sharing one log, and does an identity that is ABSENT change nothing, on W5's ownership verdict as well as on W3 and `next`", since absence is exactly the state that produces the false red.

THE ORDER. INC1 IS FIRST AND ALONE, on two grounds: it is the only member that blocks a step today, and the pass established that it ships without coupling to the rest, since direction (iii) adds no field to any struct and so is not bound by the one-deliberate-edit constraint that governs the other members. INC2 FOLLOWS IT because it is a claim about the same function that inc1 has just changed, and the cheapest moment to state the reachability of one rule truthfully is while its sibling is fresh. INC3, INC4 AND INC5 ARE INDEPENDENT of each other and of inc1; the order between them is NOT load-bearing and is stated as a default rather than a constraint, so re-ordering them needs no decision. INC6 IS LAST AMONG THE DECLARED INCREMENTS, and this edge IS load-bearing: the human's recorded constraint is that the record schema takes ONE deliberate edit, the prospective waiver-note join needs `valid_findings` on the same struct, and whether that join is built at all is undecided. Landing the schema edit before that is decided risks being the first of two edits, which is the thing the constraint exists to prevent. INC6 THEREFORE HAS AN ENTRY GATE: put the note-join question to the human before it starts.

INC6'S FOURTH LIMITATION IS NOT A REASON TO RE-ORDER, and it is recorded here so a later reader does not read it as one. The measured fact runs the other way: `check_workflow_toml` computes the rounds at one site and hands them to `run_checks`, so a filter applied there is inherited by every check that reads them, and TODAY W5 READS NONE, so an identity filter would not protect W5's ownership verdict at all. Under direction (iii) it would. INC1 THEREFORE STRICTLY IMPROVES THE COVERAGE of the queued identity edit rather than complicating it, which the architecture lens measured at `docs/plans/validation-constraints.explorations/Q-70-architecture.md:296` and `:336`. What the fourth limitation adds is a case inc6's own review must cover, not an argument for landing inc6 first.

## The three detection mechanisms

NONE OF THE THREE HAS A DECLARED INCREMENT, and that is deliberate rather than an omission. They are in this step's scope by the human's `Q-55-entryroute` decision, which this step relays and does not reopen. What the pass ruled about each is recorded here so the eventual build starts from it.

MECHANISM 1, THE WAIVER-NOTE BREAKDOWN JOIN, checking a waiver note's `<total> (<r1>, <r2>, ...)` per-round breakdown against the `valid_findings` of that increment's round records. IT IS A REGRESSION GUARD, NOT A DEFECT FINDER: every breakdown currently in the plan agrees with the records. Re-measured for this fold: enumerate the breakdowns with `grep -onE "[(][0-9]+(, [0-9]+){1,6}[)]" docs/plans/agent-scaffold.plan.toml` and compare each against `jq -r --arg t <increment-id> 'select(.type=="round" and ((.increment // .task)==$t)) | .valid_findings' docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl`; every one agreed. NO COUNT OF THE NOTE SITES IS STATED, because the population grows with every escalated loop that earns a waiver. ITS JOIN IS THE PREDICATE INC1 BUILDS, so under the decided direction the join costs nothing; ITS DATA IS NOT SHARED, since `Round` carries no `valid_findings` and `parse_rounds` (`src/metrics.rs:660-711`) discards it even though `check_record` requires it in the raw record. That data half is the coupling the human's one-deliberate-edit constraint governs, and it belongs with inc6 if it is built at all. WHETHER IT IS BUILT IS NOT DECIDED.

MECHANISM 2, DANGLING DECISION-RECEIPT DETECTION. ITS RED LIST IS EMPTY TODAY under the parent-resolution reading, so it too is a regression guard rather than a defect finder. THE SUB-DECISION RULING, which all three explorers reached independently and which changes what the mechanism is: a receipt `q_id` of the form `Q-<n>-<suffix>` whose parent `Q-<n>` is registered is a LEGITIMATE SUB-DECISION CONVENTION, not a dangling receipt. Re-measured for this fold, and the figure had already moved since the explorations were written, which is why no figure is repeated here: extract the receipt ids with `jq -r 'select(.type=="decision") | .q_id' docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl | sort -u`, extract the registered ids with `grep -oE '^id = "Q-[^"]+"' docs/plans/agent-scaffold.plan.toml`, take the set difference, and check the two properties rather than the size: every unresolved id is `Q-<n>-<suffix>` shaped, and every parent `Q-<n>` is registered. Both held. The pass's own measurement that every unresolved id shared the single parent `Q-55` NO LONGER HOLDS, because `Q-70-resolver` was written the same day; the STRUCTURAL property survived the change and the enumeration did not, which is the whole argument for stating properties rather than sets. A detector built without the parent clause would be red on the project's own dominant convention.

MECHANISM 3, THE QUOTATION RESOLVER, is BOUNDED BY THIS STEP AND DESIGNED LATER, by the human's `Q-70-resolver` decision. It is the only one of the three that reaches the dangling-quotation class, which no gate in this repository catches. A DESIGN PASS IS OWED BEFORE IT IS BUILT; when that pass runs and who registers it are not settled here. Its three measured design constraints, recorded so the later pass starts from them rather than rediscovering them:

- ITS OPENING RED LIST IS THE WHOLE STALE-CITATION SET, not a subset. `Q-70` records that every distinct `src/checks.rs` citation in `docs/plans/agent-scaffold.steps/checks-runner-worktree-name-collision.md` resolves to unrelated content in the current source, because that step's own fix replaced the code the sidecar cites, and two explorers spot-checked that claim without finding an exception. `Q-55-check21b` ruled those deliberately left stale and that ruling stands. Enumerate them with `grep -oE "src/checks[.]rs:[0-9]+(-[0-9]+)?" docs/plans/agent-scaffold.steps/checks-runner-worktree-name-collision.md | sort -u`, then open each at the line. A resolver whose first run reproduces an already-recorded fact has not yet earned its cost, so the pass must say what the mechanism does about an accepted-stale citation.
- THE SELF-QUOTING RECORD (constraint 3a). A resolver that asks only "does this quoted string occur in the cited file" GOES GREEN ON THE EXACT CLASS IT EXISTS FOR as soon as the record writes the defect down: when an edit deletes a sentence, the deleted sentence comes to occur again inside the post-mortem OF the deletion, so the dangling quotation resolves. A resolver must scope to LIVE passages and exclude a record's own post-mortems and round records. THIS PROJECT QUOTES ITSELF AS A MATTER OF PRACTICE, so the case is not rare, and the constraint is not confined to the ledger: it has already fired inside the `Q-70` item itself, which is why that item's own control command is corrected in the same fold that authors this step.
- EXPECTED TOOL OUTPUT IS NOT A DOCUMENT QUOTATION (constraint 3b). The validator problem strings `Q-70` quotes from its own fixtures are runtime-substituted format output and exist in full nowhere but that item and its rendered projection; the format string that produces one of them is at `src/plan/source.rs:809`. A resolver with no expected-output escape reports the item's strongest evidence as dangling. Verify with a fixed-string grep for either quoted problem string across the tree.

## The naming collision, and how this step writes it

"W6" ALREADY NAMES TWO DISTINCT UNBUILT CHECKS in the durable record: the waiver-note breakdown join above, and `Q-59`'s `session_state` transition-legality check, whose richer lifecycle state the human's 2026-07-23 decision DEFERRED behind an evidence gate rather than dropped, so the collision does not lapse on its own. Re-measured for this fold: the token `W6` occurs in `docs/plans/agent-scaffold.plan.toml` exactly once outside the `Q-70` item, and that occurrence is `Q-59`'s. THIS FILE THEREFORE NEVER USES "W6" TO NAME A CHECK. It writes "the waiver-note breakdown join" and "`Q-59`'s transition-legality check". Neither check is renumbered by this step; both are unbuilt, and a collision between two unbuilt checks costs nothing until one ships, at which point whoever ships first assigns the number once with the other claim visible. SEPARATELY AND NOT TO BE CONFLATED: the two owed waiver ids `workflow-enforcement-tier-w5` and `-w6` are WAIVER IDS continuing that step's established `-w1` to `-w4` sequence, not check names. The waiver-id convention is established and is not the thing to change.

## Risk classification

Classified once, here, so the required clean-round count is a recorded property of each artifact rather than a fresh judgement each round.

`validation-constraints-inc1` is RISKY (two consecutive clean rounds). It changes the verdict of the check the project's whole enforcement tier rests on, and its failure mode is not a crash but a confident wrong answer in either direction: a false green admits a waiver that grants an exemption nothing evidences, and a false red blocks a correct plan. It ships a KNOWN NARROWING of what a waiver may cover, which is a deliberate break rather than a strict tightening, and the narrowing's exact boundary is the one point the design pass left open, so the review has to judge a decision the implementer makes rather than only the code. It also edits three drift-guarded prose copies of a rule that ships into every scaffolded project, and this project's calibration on prose that states an enforcement boundary is its worst measured class. The counter-argument, that the code half is about thirty lines in one file and two explorers ran the full suite green on it, is about diff size and not blast radius, which this project has recorded losing before.

`validation-constraints-inc2` is RISKY (two consecutive clean rounds). Its cheapest treatment is a claim about a check's reachability on two substrates, which is a documentation-claim surface, and its other treatment edits `w5_problems` again immediately after inc1 changed it. A wrong claim here is worse than no claim: it would tell a reader that a rule guards something it cannot guard. THE `B5` FOLD DOES NOT CHANGE THE CLASS AND IS NOT A REASON TO RE-CLASSIFY: it adds one test against an existing clause, and the classification already rests on the increment editing `w5_problems` and asserting what a rule guards, which is exactly what `B5` asks it to pin.

`validation-constraints-inc3` is RISKY (two consecutive clean rounds). The containment TOCTOU is a guard whose failure is a `workflow invariants hold` at exit 0 over a log outside the project root, which is the false-green class this whole cluster exists to remove, and a race is not established by the obvious test. The mode-000 member changes exit codes on an error path, which is the externally depended-on contract. The two message members touch what `validate` tells a user to do when it cannot read an input, and both sit on the gate a human decision already declined to move, so the increment can reach a decision rather than only a fix.

`validation-constraints-inc4` is RISKY (two consecutive clean rounds). `next` emits an INSTRUCTION that an agent acts on, so a wrong answer is not a wrong report but a wrong action, and the worst of the defects it carries already caused exactly that: it advised marking a step complete over committed unbuilt work.

`validation-constraints-inc5` is RISKY (two consecutive clean rounds), and the ground it was FIRST given was false. That first ground was that nothing reads `blocked_by`, so a wrong value would be inert; the plan review falsified it in one command, and the reader inventory is in the increment's own bullet above. The correct ground is the opposite one: every treatment in this increment's fork changes something a reader already consumes. A populated blocker rewrites the Notes cell of a Roadmap row in the generated view, so `render --check` moves with it; and it can flip which step `next` recommends, which is an INSTRUCTION an agent acts on, the same reason inc4 is `risky`. The uncaught case is what decides the class: a blocker naming a REAL but WRONG step passes `validate_source`'s self-reference and dangling-slug checks, passes every other gate this repository owns, and silently changes what `next` tells the next agent to do. THE ESCAPE HATCH THAT PREVIOUSLY CARRIED THIS IS DELETED RATHER THAN REPHRASED: it said to re-classify if the treatment "also teaches `next` to honour the field", and `next` already honours it, so that trigger could never fire and the increment would have converged at one clean round on a premise two commands falsify. The classification is now made once, here, as the convergence rule requires, and it does not depend on which treatment is chosen. THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT, recorded because it is real and was weighed: the increment is scoped to plan content, a dangling or self-referential blocker IS caught, and the change is reversible in one revert. It loses to the uncaught real-but-wrong case, which no gate catches and which changes an agent's next action.

`validation-constraints-inc6` is RISKY (two consecutive clean rounds). It edits the record schema W3, W4 and W5 all read, under an explicit human constraint about how that edit is made, and it changes `project_root_of_source`, through which every command's path resolution flows. Its own recorded limitations mean a naive filter placement leaves `next` unprotected while appearing to protect everything, which is a silent partial fix.

## Acceptance check

THE LIST HAS TWO KINDS OF ITEM AND THEY ARE SETTLED DIFFERENTLY, so each item says which it is rather than leaving the reader to infer it from an opening claim that does not hold of all of them. A COMMAND item is a command with an expected exit code and is settled by running it, not by reading the diff. A REPORT OBLIGATION is a statement the round report must make and is settled by the report; it is marked as one at the item, and it is not dressed up as a command it cannot be. `Q-66` applies: a behavioural claim owes a demonstration that is RED against the pre-fix build and green after, and the round report names which mutation or which pre-fix revision produced the red. THE LIST IS A FLOOR AND NOT A TOTAL, and no total is stated: every fix round that closes a defect owes its own red-then-green beside these.

BEFORE RUNNING ANY OF THIS: point `TMPDIR` at a directory OUTSIDE any git repository. Three of the suite's tests assert their scratch directory is not inside a repository, so a worktree-internal `TMPDIR` fails them spuriously. That is a property of the suite, held by its own step `test-tmpdir-repo-assumption`, and it is not a regression here.

1. COMMAND. Build, suite and lint: `cargo build`, `cargo test`, and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, all clean. WHAT THE DRIFT GUARD IN THAT SUITE DOES AND DOES NOT COVER, stated here because naming it without saying so reads as rule-text coverage and it is not: `the_committed_scaffold_matches_a_fresh_render` compares the committed `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/AGENTS.reference.md` against a FRESH RENDER OF THE PACK, so it catches a PARTIAL prose edit and a stale pack source, and it never reads `src/`, so it is structurally blind to prose that still states a rule the code no longer implements. The rule text's currency is item 7b, not this item. AND ONE MIGRATION OBLIGATION INSIDE THIS SUITE, which is load-bearing and is not left to taste: the existing test `w5_flags_an_increment_waiver_whose_step_does_not_own_its_increment` (find it with `grep -n "fn w5_flags_an_increment_waiver_whose_step_does_not_own_its_increment" src/workflow.rs`; the line span this item used to cite predates inc1 and moved when inc1 landed) MUST KEEP ITS SUBJECT, so once the rule is structural its fixture must carry round records that establish the increment's true owner, and it must still assert a mis-scoping. A migration that instead leaves the fixture with no round records silently converts the only existing test for this rule into a test of the UNOBSERVED case and moves nothing but its message; the plan review measured that both migrations conform to this list as it was first written, and that the lax one lets a build which accepts an observed contradiction pass the whole suite. Note also that item 7 pins that the predicate is SHARED and not that W5 quantifies over the right thing, so item 7 is not the catch for this class either; item 4b is.
2. COMMAND. AFTER INC1, THE LIVE PLAN IS UNCHANGED IN VERDICT, which is the no-regression check: `agent-scaffold validate --source docs/plans/agent-scaffold.plan.toml --workflow` exits 0 with `workflow invariants hold`, with every waiver already committed to this plan satisfying the new rule and NO edit to any waiver and NO edit to the append-only log. IT IS NOT A MIGRATION PROOF AND MUST NOT BE READ AS ONE: it is green on the pre-fix binary, on a correct fix, and on a build with the rule deleted outright, so it has no red half and demonstrates nothing about the fix. What it does establish is a PRECONDITION, that the population the narrowing affects is empty on this plan.
3. COMMAND. AFTER INC1, THE BLOCKED STEP UNBLOCKS: with both fold tokens declared as `[[step.increment]]` entries, both owed waivers written, and `workflow-enforcement-tier` at `complete`, the same command exits 0 with `workflow invariants hold`. Against the pre-fix binary the identical tree exits non-zero on the ownership rule alone, and the round report quotes both.
4. COMMAND. AFTER INC1, THE UNOBSERVED CASE IS PINNED AS A DECISION, not left implicit. THIS ITEM PINS THE UNOBSERVED CASE ONLY, that is, an increment-unit waiver whose increment has NO round records anywhere; the OBSERVED contradiction is pinned by item 4b whichever form is taken here, and that separation is deliberate, because the silent branch below is satisfied by a build with no ownership rule at all and would otherwise swallow the case where the rule does its only work. THE RECEIPT PUT THREE OPTIONS AND NOT TWO, and an earlier form of this item said "two forms", which could not pin a decision taken over three: `Q-70-emptycase` (human, 2026-08-12) presented REPORT IT, STAY SILENT ON IT, and REPORT IT BUT ONLY WHEN THE LOG IS NON-EMPTY, and chose REPORT IT. A test pins the decision only if it distinguishes the chosen form from BOTH declined ones, and the third option is the one a test against an empty rounds slice alone cannot separate from the first. Under the reporting form such a waiver is REPORTED and the test asserts the message, on a log that carries records for other increments AND on a log that carries none; under the silent form it PASSES W5 and the test asserts that `src/plan/source.rs`'s membership check still catches the undeclared case, plus the residual that a DECLARED and never-logged increment passes. INC1 SHIPPED THE REPORTING FORM, pinned by `w5_flags_an_increment_waiver_whose_increment_has_no_round_records` on a non-empty log and by `w5_flags_an_increment_waiver_when_the_round_log_carries_no_records_at_all` on an empty one, which is the pair that separates option one from option three.
4b. COMMAND. AFTER INC1, AN OBSERVED CONTRADICTION IS REFUSED, on BOTH substrates. An increment-unit waiver whose increment's round records join it to a DIFFERENT step must be REPORTED, and the round report quotes the fixture and the message. THE RED HALF IS A MUTATION, NOT THE PRE-FIX BINARY, and this is the item's whole point: the pre-fix binary refuses this case too, by accident of the lexical rule, so it cannot supply the red. The mutation is THE STEP AXIS DROPPED ON W5'S SIDE of the shared predicate, that is, W5 passing the waiver's own `step` where the correct implementation passes the step the round record carries, so the comparison degenerates to comparing a value with itself. That build is a REGRESSION AGAINST THE SHIPPED TOOL, and the plan review measured it passing every other item in this list, including item 7's own demonstration, while accepting at exit 0 a tree both the pre-fix binary and a correct fix refuse. It passes item 1 only under the lax migration of the test item 1 now pins, which is why that pinning and this item are two independent catches rather than one. A worked fixture is a Markdown plan with two `complete` steps plus a JSONL log in which the waived increment's round records all carry the OTHER step, which is item 6's fixture with a second step and one changed field. THIS OBLIGATION IS INDEPENDENT OF ITEM 4'S FORK and holds under both the reporting form and the silent form.
4c. COMMAND. AFTER INC1, THE INCREMENT AXIS OF THE SHARED PREDICATE IS PINNED ON BOTH CONSUMERS. It sits beside 4b because 4b pins the STEP axis and, until this item was added, nothing on the list reached the other one, which is how a build with the increment axis dropped passed the whole list while returning `workflow invariants hold` at exit 0 over an unconverged `risky` increment, and over a tree the pre-fix binary also refuses. Demonstrate by mutation: drop the increment comparison from the shared predicate and show that a W3 test and a W5 test both go red. In the suite today that pair is `an_increment_waiver_does_not_exempt_a_sibling_increment_of_the_same_step` on W3's side and `w5_flags_an_increment_waiver_whose_increment_has_no_round_records` on W5's, and the second only reaches the axis because its fixture carries a NON-EMPTY log; an empty rounds slice cannot distinguish "no records for this increment" from "no records at all". THIS ITEM IS THE LIST'S CATCH AND NOT THE SUITE'S: inc1's fix passes added the tests, and the item exists so a later change to this code is still measured against the axis rather than against whatever the suite happens to hold.

Reproduce the item's own fixture, a waiver naming an increment no round record resolves to, and confirm W5 says the round log joins it to no step rather than naming a step derived from the id. THE SCOPE IS THE EMPTY-OWNERS BRANCH ALONE, and the correction matters because the unscoped form of this sentence is false of the shipped tool: on the NON-EMPTY branch W5 still names a step that `round_step_slug`'s fallback computed, deliberately, and marks it as derived from a record's `task` so the refusal never offers a computed step as a recorded one. The three inputs are WHICH RECORDS ENTER THE SCAN, WHICH STRUCTURED FIELD DECIDES THE MARK, and WHETHER THE MERGE IS ORDER-INDEPENDENT. Mutate each in turn and show a test goes red for each. Two of the three mutations are killed by one fixture, a record carrying a structured `increment` and no `step` whose `task` DIFFERS from the increment id; the third needs the two log lines in both orders, because a suite whose only mixed-case fixture puts the declaring record first cannot tell a union from first-write-wins. The pre-fix binary refuses a correctly-scoped waiver there and the fixed binary accepts it, so the fix is not TOML-only. That matters here more than anywhere else, because inc2 records that the JSONL substrate is the one where a mis-scoped waiver's `step` is independently authorable and so the one where the rule can actually fire.

If only one goes red, the predicate was copied rather than shared. This pins SHARING and not what W5 quantifies over, so it is not the catch for a dropped step axis; item 4b is.
7b. COMMAND. AFTER INC1, THE SHIPPED RULE TEXT MATCHES THE SHIPPED BEHAVIOUR. Two fixed-string commands over all three copies, so a partial edit fails: `grep -c -F "the increment's leading slug equals the step" pack/instrument.md AGENTS.md .agents/AGENTS.reference.md` must report 0 for each of the three, and a fixed-string check for the replacement must report 1 for each. THE REPLACEMENT CHECK NAMES THE WHOLE PARENTHETICAL AND NOT ONE STRING INSIDE IT, because the sentence around it has moved twice and a fragment stays green while the rest of the clause drifts:

```
RULE='(some `round` record must join that increment to that step, resolving each axis exactly as the escalation join below does; an increment no `round` record resolves to is reported, and an owning step that no record of that increment declares in a structured `step` id is reported as derived, since such a step need not appear in the Roadmap or anywhere in the log)'
grep -c -F "$RULE" pack/instrument.md AGENTS.md .agents/AGENTS.reference.md
```

Single quotes are required around the value, because the parenthetical carries backticks. THE RED HALF IS THE PRE-FIX TREE, where the first command reports 1 for each. BOTH COMMANDS ARE PATH-SCOPED TO THOSE THREE FILES AND MUST STAY SO: the retired wording occurs in this sidecar, in the rendered plan view, in the exploration files and in the review records, all of which quote it while discussing the change, and the replacement wording now occurs in this sidecar and in the rendered view as well, because the item above quotes it in full. A tree-wide form of either check would therefore report a hit forever and never mean anything. That is constraint (3a), the self-quoting record, applied to the step's own check rather than only described by it. This item exists because no other check covers it: the plan review built six behaviour-changing variants of the fix, and every one left all three copies stating the retired lexical rule while the whole suite reported green, since the drift guard compares the committed copies against a fresh render of the pack and never reads `src/`. The text ships into every scaffolded project, so a green here that means nothing is a green in every project this tool scaffolds.

The fixtures the ledger already records are a mode-000 log FILE against an unsearchable DIRECTORY over the same log; a FIFO-widened mid-run symlink swap that must no longer yield `workflow invariants hold` at exit 0 over a log outside the project root; the `no metrics log at <path>` note printing above the corrected sentence; and a mode-600 `docs/plans` yielding a message whose remedy is aimed at someone who already passed a source. 11. COMMAND. AFTER INC4, `next` no longer recommends a completion its own step's brief contradicts, it no longer emits the ledger's resume state verbatim, and a run with no `--source` fails loudly rather than exiting calmly. THE OUTPUT-SIZE CLAUSE IS DELIBERATELY NOT A THRESHOLD: "proportionate" had no measurement and two reviewers could reach opposite verdicts on it with nothing to settle between them, so what is pinned is the verbatim dump, which is a fixed-string test, and the round report states the measured output size before and after without a bound. Setting a bound is a decision nobody has made.
12. REPORT OBLIGATION. AFTER INC5, the structured source encodes the ordering: the round report states the treatment taken and shows that the answer `next` gives about which step is next follows from the structured source rather than from ledger prose.
13. REPORT OBLIGATION. AFTER INC6, a declared identity separates two projects sharing one merged log, and an ABSENT identity changes nothing. The round report states which surfaces the filter placement does and does not cover, naming `next` AND W5, since after inc1 W5 reads the same rounds slice. The absent-identity case must be exercised against a plan carrying at least one increment-unit waiver, because that is the case where an over-broad filter turns a correct plan red rather than merely leaving a surface uncovered.

## Scope: what this step does not do

- It does not reshape the waiver schema. No nesting of a waiver under an increment, no collapsing of the unit field, no change to the JSONL waiver arm, no rewrite of the committed waivers. The precondition for encoding ownership positionally is a declared increment set that models the identities the checks operate on, and that set is hand-maintained and derived from nothing; compare `jq -r 'select(.type=="round") | (.increment // .task)' docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl | sort -u` against the declared `[[step.increment]]` ids before assuming otherwise. Two logged identities cannot be declared at all under `is_kebab_case_token` (`src/plan/source.rs:475-477`), which forbids an uppercase byte and is pinned by `an_uppercase_increment_id_is_flagged`, while the round log uses an `-incA`/`-incB` form.
- It does not widen `plan::Step`. It is `Serialize` and is the `status --json` payload, so widening it changes a machine output contract, and nothing in the decided direction needs it. This is also why the declared-increment lookup (direction (i)) is not the fix: it would feed W5 data only one substrate possesses, against the parity property `src/next.rs:517-523` records.
- It does not make the ownership rule substrate-conditional and does not retire it. `run_checks` is deliberately ONE implementation across both substrates (`src/workflow.rs:196-200`, stated as Principle 16), and the decided direction keeps it that way.
- It does not derive the declared increment set from the round log, or rule on what a declared increment is FOR. That is a separate step and its precondition is undiagnosed.
- It does not build the waiver-note breakdown join, the dangling-receipt detector, or the quotation resolver. The first two have empty red lists today and neither is decided; the third is bounded here by the human's decision and owed a design pass.
- It does not renumber either unbuilt check, and it does not rename the `-w5` and `-w6` waiver ids.
- It does not register the `Q-<n>-<suffix>` receipt ids as questions. Under the sub-decision ruling they are a convention a detector models, not defects to be cured by registration.
- It does not rewrite, re-key or re-model the append-only round log. Every direction that required that was ruled out.
- It does not rename any already-declared increment id. Under the decided direction the `workflow-driver` trio joins correctly as it stands.
- It does not claim ownership of the ledger half of the `run_next` false green. That input has no owner in the plan and is carried above rather than scheduled.

### Defect `F1`: `render` interpolates free-text TOML into generated Markdown unescaped

Verified against the source at `a4394e4`, not against a summary. `escape_cell` (`src/plan/render.rs:538`) neutralises `|` and every line-ending form, and it is called at ONE site, `src/plan/render.rs:467`, the Roadmap Notes cell. Three further sites interpolate free-text TOML into the generated Markdown with no neutralisation at all:

- `src/plan/render.rs:296`, `[meta].title` into the `# <title> plan` heading.
- `src/plan/render.rs:402`, `principle.name` and `principle.text` into the numbered Project Principles list.
- `src/plan/render.rs:436`, `question.ask` into the Open-Questions queue line, which `src/plan/render.rs:424` documents as "strictly ONE line per item".

So the generated document's STRUCTURE is controlled by the source's free TEXT, and a `.plan.toml` that `validate --source` accepts can render a `<task>.md` that `validate --plan` rejects. Principle 8 (Structured data first, project for humans) is the principle this breaks: a projection that the projecting tool's own validator refuses is not a projection.

REPRODUCTION (written by this planning pass; the audit record carries none). Copy the render fixture out of the source tree, give one question a two-line `ask` whose second line looks like a queue item, then render and validate:

```
cp -r src/plan/testdata/render-fixture.* /tmp/f1/
# in /tmp/f1/render-fixture.plan.toml, replace Q-1's ask with:
#   ask = """An open ask still awaiting a decision.
#   - `Q-42` (undecided) a queue item nobody authored."""
cargo run -- validate --source /tmp/f1/render-fixture.plan.toml --metrics /dev/null
cargo run -- render /tmp/f1/render-fixture.plan.toml
cargo run -- validate --plan /tmp/f1/render-fixture.md --metrics /dev/null
```

Measured at `a4394e4`: `validate --source` reports "7 steps, 5 questions, valid" at exit 0, `render` writes the projection, and `validate --plan` reports "Open Questions item `Q-42` has an unknown status `undecided`" at exit 1. `Q-42` is in no `[[question]]` entry. A blank line in an `ask` produces the quieter form of the same defect: the queue list fragments and the trailing prose lands loose between items, which no check reports at all.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA for `F1`, each executable:

1. Red then green on the reproduction above. Before the fix `validate --plan` reports the fabricated `Q-42`; after it, the same source renders a projection whose queue carries exactly the `[[question]]` ids the source declares, and `validate --plan` says nothing about `Q-42`. The reproduction lands as a test, so the red state cannot return silently.
2. All four interpolation sites are covered, not only the queue. A test pins each of `src/plan/render.rs:296`, `:402`, `:436` and `:467` against a source whose corresponding free-text field carries a line ending, a `|`, and a leading `- ` list marker, and asserts the generated line count and the generated structure are what the source's STRUCTURE implies.
3. `render --check --strict docs/plans/agent-scaffold.plan.toml` reports up to date after the live projection is regenerated in the same change. The live projection WILL change: many live `ask` values are multi-paragraph, so they currently fragment the queue and will collapse to one line each. That is the contract being restored, not a regression.
4. `validate --plan docs/plans/agent-scaffold.md --metrics docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl` reports EXACTLY ONE problem afterwards, the pre-existing "Open Questions item `Q-43` has an unknown status `superseded by `Q-44``". That problem is NOT `F1` and is out of this step's scope: `question_status_display` (`src/plan/render.rs:445`) emits `superseded by <slug>` while `question_status_ok` (`src/plan.rs:378`) accepts only the exact statuses plus the `decided -> folded into ` prefix, so the two vocabularies disagree independently of any escaping. It is recorded here so a reviewer neither mistakes it for an `F1` escape nor widens the step to fix it.

FIX DIRECTION, recommended with its reasoning, and the alternative named. Neutralise every free-text value at the point where it is interpolated into a generated line, extending the one-line rule `escape_cell` already applies to the Notes cell, and keep the `|` escape for table cells where it matters. The alternative is to reject a multi-line `ask` in `validate --source` and move that prose into the question sidecars, which is the stronger Principle 5 form (Make illegal states unrepresentable). It is not taken here because it relocates prose across about twenty questions, which is exactly the churn this step exists to avoid (Principle 2, Minimal by default), and it stays available to a later step. State which was chosen in the outcome.

### Defect `F4`: a pack `dest` can write outside `--output-dir`

Verified against the source at `a4394e4`. `src/manifest.rs:46` documents `AssetSpec.dest` as "Destination path relative to the output directory" and `src/manifest.rs:271` says the same of `Asset.dest`. No containment check exists in `src/manifest.rs`, and the write site, `apply_asset` (`src/main.rs:119`), is a bare `root.join(&asset.dest)`, which a `..` component escapes and an absolute path discards the root of entirely. The run then reports "Wrote to `<output-dir>`".

Principle 3 (Safe on existing projects) is the principle this breaks: scaffolding must never clobber or silently overwrite existing files, and a write the tool reports as landing inside the output directory while it lands outside is that failure in its least visible form.

REPRODUCTION (written by this planning pass; the audit record carries none). Two shapes, both measured at `a4394e4`:

```
mkdir -p /tmp/f4/pack /tmp/f4/out
printf 'x\n' > /tmp/f4/pack/escape.md
printf '[[asset]]\nsource = "escape.md"\ndest = "../../escaped-outside.md"\nownership = "working"\n' > /tmp/f4/pack/pack.toml
cargo run -- scaffold --template /tmp/f4/pack --output-dir /tmp/f4/out --vcs none --write
```

Measured: exit 0, the plan line reads `create  ../../escaped-outside.md`, the summary reads "Wrote to /tmp/f4/out (1 changed, 0 left untouched)", and the file lands at `/tmp/escaped-outside.md`. Replacing the `dest` with an absolute path reproduces the same result with the absolute destination printed verbatim.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA for `F4`, each executable:

1. Red then green on both shapes above. Before the fix each writes outside `--output-dir` at exit 0; after it each is refused at a non-zero exit, the message names the offending `dest`, and nothing is written anywhere, inside or outside. Both land as tests.
2. The refusal happens when the manifest is loaded, before any write and before the plan preview is printed, so `--dry-run` cannot preview an escaping asset either and the preview never promises a write the action refuses.
3. The predicate is not authored twice. `is_safe_sidecar_ref` (`src/plan/source.rs:488`) already rejects an absolute path and any `..` component, for this exact reason, and is private to `plan::source`. The fix either lifts it to a shared home or records why a second copy is correct (Principle 1, Prefer the cleaner long-term architecture over the smallest diff).
4. Nothing else moves: `cargo test` passes with the built-in asset list at `src/manifest.rs:611` unchanged, and a normal `scaffold` run drops the same set of files it dropped before.

MAKE THE CLAIM TRUE RATHER THAN DELETE IT, recommended. Deleting the claim is cheaper and is what `src/checks.rs:17-26` does for `.agents/checks.toml`, arguing the trusted-config boundary explicitly. That argument does not carry over: a `.agents/checks.toml` is authored by the user in their own repository, whereas `--template` names a pack the user may have fetched from anywhere, so the pack is external input rather than the user's own configuration. Principle 3 (Safe on existing projects) settles it, and rejecting at the boundary rather than guarding at the write is Principle 5 (Make illegal states unrepresentable). If the implementer takes the delete option instead, the doc comments at `src/manifest.rs:46` and `:271` must stop saying "relative to the output directory" and the README must state the real contract, so the step still closes the gap between what is claimed and what holds.

### Defect `F4b`: a pack `source` can read outside the pack directory

NOT an audit finding. It was found during this step's own implementation of `F4`, reported rather than fixed, and admitted here by `Q-75` (human, 2026-08-13), which is the one authorised widening of the scope above. The number carries `4` because it is the read-side twin of `F4`, in the same struct and closed by the same predicate, and the letter because the audit's `F1` to `F4` numbering is a closed record this defect is not part of.

Verified against the source at `d06f1b5`, whose `src/` is identical to `a4394e4`. `src/manifest.rs:44` documents `AssetSpec.source` as "Path of the source file within the pack". Nothing enforces that. The read site, `PackSource::Directory::read` (`src/manifest.rs:307`), is a bare `fs::read_to_string(root.join(rel))`, which a `..` component escapes and an absolute path discards the root of entirely, exactly as `apply_asset` does on the write side. Two callers pass pack-controlled text to it: `src/manifest.rs:532` (`spec.source`, once per asset) and `src/manifest.rs:433` (`module.guidance`, once per enabled module). The three literal callers (`pack.toml`, `principles.toml`, `instrument.md`) pass fixed strings and are not affected.

Principle 5 (Make illegal states unrepresentable) is the principle this breaks: a doc comment declares the state illegal and no code makes that true, which is the admit-then-guard shape the principle exists to prevent, except that here nothing guards either. Principle 1 (Prefer the cleaner long-term architecture over the smallest diff) is what settles it inside this step rather than after it: once `F4` lands, `AssetSpec` enforces containment on `dest` and not on `source`, which is an incoherent boundary rather than a smaller one.

REPRODUCTION (measured by this planning pass at `d06f1b5`; paths shortened for legibility, the run used a scratch directory):

```
mkdir -p /tmp/f4b/pack /tmp/f4b/out
printf 'TOP SECRET\n' > /tmp/f4b/secret.md
printf '[[asset]]\nsource = "../secret.md"\ndest = "leaked.md"\nownership = "working"\n' > /tmp/f4b/pack/pack.toml
cargo run -- scaffold --template /tmp/f4b/pack --output-dir /tmp/f4b/out --vcs none --write
```

Measured: exit 0, the plan line reads `create  leaked.md`, the summary reads "Wrote to /tmp/f4b/out (1 changed, 0 left untouched)", and `/tmp/f4b/out/leaked.md` contains `TOP SECRET`. An absolute `source` reproduces the same result. Two differences from `F4` matter for the acceptance criteria. First, the `dest` is legal, so the output names only `leaked.md` and the leak is invisible in what the run reports. Second, `--dry-run` in place of `--write` prints the same `create  leaked.md` at exit 0, and the outside file has already been read by then, because `load` (`src/manifest.rs:532`) reads the contents into `Asset.contents` before any plan line is printed.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA for `F4b`, each executable:

1. Red then green on both shapes, the `..` and the absolute. Before the fix each copies an outside file into the scaffolded project at exit 0; after it each is refused at a non-zero exit, the message names the offending `source`, and nothing is written. Both land as tests.
2. `--dry-run` is refused too, and the outside file is never opened, not merely never written. This is `F4`'s criterion 2 on the read side, and here it is the whole of the defect rather than a preview detail: the read is the leak.
3. One predicate, one site. The containment predicate `F4`'s fix introduces, named `safe_path::is_contained_relative` on the implementer's branch as of this writing and absent at `d06f1b5`, is applied at the `PackSource::Directory` arm of `src/manifest.rs:307`, so `spec.source` and `module.guidance` are both covered by one application (Principle 1, Prefer the cleaner long-term architecture over the smallest diff). A fix that checks `spec.source` alone leaves `module.guidance` open and does not close this defect. `PackSource::Embedded` needs no check and gets none: its paths are compile-time and its lookup touches no filesystem. If the implementer instead rejects at manifest-parse time, the outcome must say how `module.guidance` is covered, since it is not an `[[asset]]` field.
4. Nothing else moves: `cargo test` passes with the built-in asset list unchanged, and a normal `scaffold` run drops the same set of files it dropped before.

FIX DIRECTION is settled by `Q-75` and no alternative is open. `F4`'s delete-the-claim option does not exist here: a `--template` pack is external input the user may have fetched from anywhere, so the `src/checks.rs:17-26` trusted-config argument does not carry over, and `Q-75` records the human rejecting the document-the-boundary option on that ground.

### Release mechanics

Ordering matters here, because the README's link has to resolve when the crate is published:

1. Land the three fixes (`F1`, `F4`, `F4b`) and regenerate the projection.
2. Set `Cargo.toml` `version` to `0.0.2` and close the `CHANGELOG.md` `## [Unreleased]` section as `## [0.0.2]`, dated.
3. Reserve `agent-flow` on crates.io at 0.0.2, so the README link has a target.
4. Add the two README items. crates.io treats `-` and `_` as one name, so reserving `agent-flow` also reserves `agent_flow`.
5. Publish `agent-scaffold` 0.0.2. Leave every earlier `agent-scaffold` version un-yanked.

One detail the `Q-65` checklist leaves open and this step must settle rather than assume: the checklist says to contact by opening an issue on the "`agent-flow` GitHub repository", which does not exist under that name until `rename-to-agent-flow` runs. The cheapest resolution is for the 0.0.2 README to name the current repository as the one that will carry the rename, and to link the crates.io `agent-flow` page for the crate itself. Record what was done.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA for the release half:

1. `cargo publish --dry-run` succeeds for `agent-scaffold` at 0.0.2.
2. The published README (the one in the 0.0.2 artifact, not only the one on the default branch) contains a link to `agent-flow` and a sentence stating the `agent-scaffold` name is reclaimable, with the contact route.
3. `agent-flow` resolves on crates.io at 0.0.2, and `agent-scaffold` 0.0.1 is still installable.
4. The seven gates are green on the release commit: `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `validate --source ... --metrics ...`, `validate --source ... --workflow`, `render --check --strict`, the ASCII check `LC_ALL=C grep -cP '[^\t\x20-\x7e]'` returning 0 on every changed file, and `cargo publish --dry-run`.

### Outcome

WRITTEN AFTER THE RELEASE SHIPPED, and it states what the step DID. It settles the one detail the release mechanics left open above, and it records what the release carried out rather than fixed. It adds no work, so the closed-scope sentence at the top of this file stands and this section is not an exception to it.

THE `Q-65` CONTACT ROUTE IS SETTLED, AND THE SETTLEMENT IS PERMANENT BECAUSE IT SHIPPED. The 0.0.2 README names the CURRENT repository as the one that will carry the rename, and links the crates.io `agent-flow` page for the crate, which is the resolution the release mechanics recommended. The shipped text is the README's "The `agent-flow` rename" section:

> This project is being renamed to `agent-flow`, and that crate name is reserved at <https://crates.io/crates/agent-flow>. Releases move there once the rename lands. Until then `agent-scaffold` is the crate to install, and every published `agent-scaffold` version stays installable.
>
> The `agent-scaffold` name is then free for whoever wants to reclaim it. To ask for it, open an issue on <https://github.com/nothingnesses/agent-scaffold>, the repository that will carry the `agent-flow` rename.

IT CANNOT BE REVISED WHERE IT MATTERS. `Cargo.toml` declares `readme = "README.md"`, so the file is inside the published artifact and crates.io renders it as the crate's front page, and a published version is not editable. Verified rather than assumed: the worktree `README.md` and the `README.md` extracted from the downloaded 0.0.2 tarball are byte-identical. `rename-to-agent-flow` inherits the consequence, and it is recorded on that step rather than only here, because that is the step that acts on it.

RESIDUALS ACCEPTED INTO THE RELEASE, each by a human decision, recorded so that no later round re-discovers one as a finding. This list states its members and no figure, which is the convention this plan uses for a set that can grow.

- `V4`, THE UNIVERSAL QUANTIFIER IN THE SUBCOMMAND-CLI `BREAKING` BULLET. `CHANGELOG.md` says of `agent-scaffold scaffold` that "every option 0.0.1 documented is still accepted there". The version flags are the exception. Measured on the 0.0.2 build: `agent-scaffold -V` prints the version at exit 0, while `agent-scaffold scaffold -V` and `agent-scaffold scaffold --version` both exit 2 with `error: unexpected argument`. Conventional for a subcommand CLI, and the impact is nil because the top-level form still works. Accepted as written.
- THE `src/audit.rs` MODULE DOC, WHICH IS NOW THE ONLY SURVIVING COPY OF A RETIRED CLAIM. The module doc says Increment 1 ships an empty report and leaves the signal producers to later increments, and the `records` field doc says the report is empty in Increment 1, while the doc comment on `CodeValueReport::from_source_scan`, five lines below that field, says it builds the Increment 2 report with the source scan run. Accepted by decision `Q-71-helptext`, on the ground that the crate is binary-only, with no `[lib]` section and no `src/lib.rs`, so these module docs render nowhere. RECORD IT AS A KNOWN-STALE SITE AND NOT AS A DEFECT TO HUNT AGAIN: the same claim was deleted from `CHANGELOG.md`, from `README.md` and from the `audit` help text, and this is what is left of it. Find it by its text rather than by line number, with `grep -n "Increment 1" src/audit.rs`.
- THE `CHANGELOG.md` LITERAL-NAME BULLET'S OPEN-VERSUS-CLOSED TENSION. Its first sentence introduces the files the tool reads by literal name with "among them", which reads open-ended, and a later sentence in the same bullet says "each of those two", which closes the list at two. It is pre-existing rather than authored by the release, and closing it needs the first sentence, which the human excluded from the closing pass's scope. Accepted.
- "a human decides each candidate", IN `README.md` AND IN THE `audit` SUBCOMMAND'S HELP TEXT. It names candidate kinds that no signal in this release produces. ### `audit-user-prompt`: add the `audit.md` user prompt, carrying the three disciplines that made the 2026-08-13 audit measure anything (`Q-72`)

Decided (`Q-72`, human, 2026-08-13). Blocked on `ship-v0-0-2` and sequenced before `rename-to-agent-flow`: the release comes first because it is the delivery this prompt has no claim on, and the prompt comes before the rename because the rename touches 138 files and would bury it.

The 2026-08-13 audit was invoked ad hoc. Nothing in the pack lets a user run one, so the method it used exists only in that record. This step adds `pack/user-prompts/audit.md` beside the six prompts already there, so a user can run the same kind of audit on their own project.

WHAT THE PROMPT MUST CARRY. Three disciplines, and they are the whole point of the step. A prompt that asks an agent to reflect on how the work is going produces a flattering summary, which is worse than nothing because it looks like evidence:

1. FIX THE CRITERIA BEFORE MEASURING. The criteria and the failure condition are written down and committed before any measurement runs, so they cannot be chosen to fit the result. The audit record names this as "the single control that makes this record worth anything".
2. NAME THE FAILURE CONDITION IN ADVANCE SO IT CANNOT MOVE. State what result would mean the thing being audited has failed, in falsifiable terms, before looking. The 2026-08-13 audit's condition was a conjunction of three measurable claims, each with an innocent explanation on its own, which is why the conjunction was decidable.
3. GIVE THE MEASURING TO AGENTS THAT DO NOT BENEFIT FROM THE ANSWER. The party whose work is being measured does not do the measuring. The 2026-08-13 audit used nine agents, each isolated in its own detached worktree, read-only, each told to treat the project's own ledger as hypotheses rather than facts and to prefer primary sources where the two disagree.

A fourth practice is worth carrying because the audit itself demonstrated its value: the audit reports the claims it FALSIFIED that belonged to the auditing party, on the ground that an audit which only finds other people's errors is not an audit.

SCOPE. One new pack asset and the mechanics that make it drop:

- `pack/user-prompts/audit.md`, matching the existing prompts' shape: a short explanation of when to use it, then a horizontal rule, then the copy-and-paste block with bracketed fill-ins.
- A `[[asset]]` entry in `pack/pack.toml` (source `user-prompts/audit.md`, dest `.agents/user-prompts/audit.md`, `ownership = "reference"`, matching the other six).
- The built-in asset-list test at `src/manifest.rs:611-619`.
- The README scaffolded-layout listing. Note that listing is already one prompt short of the pack: `review.md` is missing from it. Adding the missing line is inside this step because the same list is being edited; nothing else in the README is.

ONE DESIGN POINT TO SETTLE AT ENTRY, not a new question. The other five human-invoked prompts are thin triggers that restate no workflow content (Principle 1, Prefer the cleaner long-term architecture over the smallest diff), and `review.md` and `explore.md` each trigger an entry mode defined in `pack/AGENTS.md`. There are four such modes today. So the audit prompt is either a fifth entry mode with a paragraph in `pack/AGENTS.md` and a thin trigger here, or a self-contained prompt that carries its three disciplines itself. The recommendation is SELF-CONTAINED: the three disciplines are an audit METHOD rather than workflow machinery, they name no role and add no phase, and putting them in `pack/AGENTS.md` grows the shipped guidance that the audit's recommendation 8 wants cut from 7,734 words to about 2,500. Decide it in the design pass and record which was chosen; if the entry-mode form is chosen, that is a `pack/AGENTS.md` edit and the regeneration set widens to `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/AGENTS.reference.md`.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:

1. `scaffold` into an empty directory drops `.agents/user-prompts/audit.md` with the pack's content, and the asset-list test names it.
2. The prompt states all three disciplines explicitly, in a form a reader can act on, not as a summary of them.
3. The prompt restates no workflow content that `pack/AGENTS.md` already owns, or, if the entry-mode form was chosen, `pack/AGENTS.md` owns the mode and the prompt only triggers it. Check by reading both, not by word count.
4. The default scaffold is otherwise byte-identical: `cargo test` passes, and a scaffold with no module selected drops the same set of files plus this one.
5. The README layout lists every prompt the pack ships, `review.md` included.

### Outcome

WRITTEN AFTER THE STEP CLOSED, and it states what shipped, what was accepted rather than fixed, and what was routed elsewhere. It adds no work. The residuals below are recorded so that no later round re-discovers one as a finding; each was checked against the shipped `pack/user-prompts/audit.md` by this closing pass rather than carried over from a summary.

THE DESIGN POINT SETTLED SELF-CONTAINED. `pack/user-prompts/audit.md` carries the three disciplines itself and triggers no entry mode, so `pack/AGENTS.md` was not edited and the regeneration set stayed at the new asset alone. The ground recorded on the change is that the disciplines are an audit method rather than workflow machinery: they name no role, add no phase, and reuse none of the review loop, so the shipped guidance has nothing to own here, and a mode paragraph would grow guidance the 2026-08-13 audit's recommendation 8 wants cut (Prefer the cleaner long-term architecture over the smallest diff; Minimal by default). The README scaffolded-layout block lists all seven prompts, `review.md` included, which acceptance criterion 5 required.

THE STEP CLOSED ON A CLEAN ROUND RATHER THAN A WAIVER, which is why this file records no exemption. Two work-review rounds and then a targeted check in place of a third round, by human decision, reached a streak of 1 against the 1 its `low_risk` class needs, so `validate --workflow` accepted the flip with no waiver written.

RESIDUALS ACCEPTED RATHER THAN FIXED. This list states its members and no figure, the convention this plan uses for a set that can grow. `B3` and `B4` were filed, triaged and accepted by decision; `D3` and `D10` were recorded by the round-3 verifier and deliberately not filed. A NOTE ON THE LABELS BEFORE THEY ARE HUNTED: `B3` and `B4` are traceable to the fix commit `4f4905f`, which names them, whereas `D3` and `D10` are the labels the verifier reported and they appear in no committed artifact, because this loop's reviewer and triage files were never committed and its record is the round entries in `docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl` plus the commit messages. Find those two by their content, stated below, rather than by grepping for their labels.

- `B3`, THE TWO PARTIES BEHIND ONE "YOU" IN PART 1. Part 1 addresses "you" throughout, and after the fresh-agent split it names two parties with that one word: the driving agent that reads the prompt and runs the audit, and the fresh agent that writes the pre-registration. The bullet "What you commit not to do. At least: not to revise this file after seeing data" is inside the list of what the pre-registration STATES, so as written the commitment is authored by, and binds, the fresh agent, which never sees data. The party that does see data is the one the commitment needs to bind. Accepted as written.
- `B4`, THE ISOLATION CLAUSE PART 1'S AGENT NEVER GETS. Part 2 gives its measuring agents both halves of the containment rule, "each in its own isolated copy and read-only against the material under audit". Part 1's fresh agent is given neither by name. The implementer declined it because part 1 is read before part 2, so borrowing those words costs either a forward reference or a duplicate, and the global rule above part 1, "Work read-only against the material under audit", already binds every part of the audit. THAT GROUND COVERS THE READ-ONLY HALF EXACTLY AND THE ISOLATION HALF NOT AT ALL: no global clause requires part 1's fresh agent to work in an isolated copy, and nothing else in the prompt supplies one. Accepted with that scope, so a later reader neither re-files the read-only half nor assumes the isolation half was covered.
- `D3`, THE QUESTION THAT TELEGRAPHS ITS OWN ANSWER, which the verifier called the only candidate worth putting to the human as an optional improvement. The `Question:` fill-in tells the human to state the test "in terms that do not indicate which answer you expect". That rule binds the human at fill-in time and no agent verifies it. Nothing in parts 1, 2 or 3 asks any agent to read the Question back and check whether it already gives the expected answer away, which is the one channel the belief can still reach part 1 through after the split closed the others. Recorded, not filed.
- `D10`, THE UNBOUNDED BINNING WIDTH. Part 2 tells the measuring agents to test a dated claim under several binnings and to report a gradual change if the date moves by more than one bin OF ANY BINNING TRIED. That phrasing makes the narrowest binning tried the binding one, which is what closed `B1`, and it bounds no binning's width. An auditor who tries only coarse binnings therefore passes the date-stability check trivially, since one coarse bin is wide enough to contain any movement the data holds. Recorded, not filed.

FOUND AROUND THIS STEP AND ROUTED OUT OF IT, so this file is not read as their home. The `audit` name now denotes two things in one product, which is `Q-77` in the queue. The two shipped-guidance gaps, `audit.md` missing from the getting-started prompt list in `pack/AGENTS.md` and the `.agents/user-prompts/` copies sitting outside the whole-file drift guard, are `user-prompts-pointer-and-drift-coverage`. Neither was fixed here.

### `rename-to-agent-flow`: rename the crate and binary from agent-scaffold to `agent-flow` at a stable release (`Q-65`)

Rename the project from `agent-scaffold` to `agent-flow` (descriptive, not a metaphor), timed to a release-ready stable state so the name can be claimed on crates.io. The identity has crossed from a scaffolding tool to a structured workflow VALIDATOR plus advisory DRIVER, with `scaffold` as one bootstrap subcommand; the name should stop mis-selling a one-shot generator (Structured data first, project for humans; Prefer the cleaner long-term architecture over the smallest diff). It is NOT a meta-harness: agents INVOKE the tool and it never runs the LLM loop, so "meta-harness" is a category error. Avoid "engine", which implies the unbuilt authoritative driver and would invite name-driven scope creep against Minimal by default.

DEFERRED because it is release-timed: land it at a stable release-ready state, not speculatively.

crates.io RELEASE CHECKLIST (durable notes):

- crates.io has NO in-place rename. Publish a NEW crate `agent-flow`: set the `Cargo.toml` `name`, the binary becomes `agent-flow`, the `scaffold` subcommand stays. Update all in-repo command examples and docs that say `agent-scaffold`.

- crates.io treats `-` and `_` as the same name, so publishing `agent-flow` also reserves `agent_flow`.
