### `workflow-audit-followups`: the 2026-08-13 audit's remaining recommendations, held as one deferred pointer rather than a backlog

Deferred, deliberately, and deliberately EMPTY of PLAN content. It holds a pointer and, since 2026-08-14, a record of measurements. It holds no work items.

The 2026-08-13 audit made ten ordered recommendations. Recommendation 1 is the release, which is `ship-v0-0-2`. Recommendations 2 to 10 stay where they were written: `docs/plans/workflow-calibration.explorations/2026-08-13-audit-when-the-loop-turned.md`, under `## Recommendations`, with the measurements that justify each of them in the sections above it. They are not copied here, not split into steps, and not summarised.

WHY THIS STEP IS A POINTER AND NOT A PLAN. The same audit measured that the share of this project's steps whose provenance is its own review process rose from 8.3% to 54.2%, monotonically, and that 74.3% of 1,022 commits touched neither product code nor tests. Turning ten recommendations into ten steps would be that mechanism running once more, at the moment the evidence for it arrived. One deferred pointer keeps them findable without creating work that then generates its own review rounds.

WHEN TO OPEN IT. After `v0.0.2` is published and `rename-to-agent-flow` has run, and then only against evidence from use rather than against the recommendations' own ordering. Read the audit record first, in full, and pick from it; do not treat this step as a queue to drain (Principle 2, Minimal by default; Principle 6, Ground decisions in evidence).

ONE THING TO CARRY FORWARD when it is opened, because it is the audit's own assessment of leverage and it is cheap to lose: recommendation 3, constraining what a fix pass may do, is the single highest-leverage variable the audit found. Deletion-only and number-edit-only fix passes re-seed findings at close to zero; fix passes that author prose re-seed at close to 100%. The project had measured that five separate times without acting on it. THAT SECOND SENTENCE IS THE AUDIT'S FRAMING AND IT IS CORRECTED TWICE BELOW, so do not stop at the first correction: mechanism 3 measured the same partition one level down and found it falls elsewhere, and mechanism 4 then measured a pass that authored no content word at all and still took a finding at each site it edited, which retires the authoring variable itself. Mechanism 4 is the one to apply.

## Measured mechanisms from the `ship-v0-0-2-inc1` review loop

CAPTURED 2026-08-14 (`Q-76`) BECAUSE THE FILES THAT HOLD THEM ARE ABOUT TO BE DELETED. Rounds 2, 3, 4 and 6 of that loop each measured a mechanism the 2026-08-13 audit does not name, each sharper than the audit's own account. Mechanism 3 corrects the audit's recommendation 3, and mechanism 4 supersedes the model mechanism 3 and the audit share. What follows is each mechanism, its measurement, and where to recover its source. It is measurement. It is not a recommendation, and it adds no work item to this step.

WHERE THE SOURCES ARE RECOVERABLE. This project commit-deletes `docs/plans/agent-scaffold.reviews/` when a loop closes, so these files will not survive the release. Each is recoverable with `git show <commit>:docs/plans/agent-scaffold.reviews/<file>` at the commit that merged it: `v002-r1-triage.md` at `281f0ad`, `v002-r2-triage.md` at `d7c9fb0`, `v002-r3-triage.md` at `306d13a`, `v002-r4-triage.md` at `01333f3`, `v002-r5-triage.md` at `8993642`, `v002-r6-triage.md` at `7ed86f8`, and `v002-verify-findings.md` at `e82e303`. The first four are present in the tree at `10d7ca2`, and every one of them at `2d78d89`. Each triager was independent of the implementer, of that round's reviewers and of the earlier triagers, and each rebuilt every number rather than citing it.

MECHANISM 1, DOMAIN WIDENING WITHOUT A CONSUMER RE-CHECK (round 2, `d7c9fb0`). The round 1 fix pass made `ReadError::Escapes` producible for ANY string, where before it was producible only for an absolute or `..`-bearing one. Two callers that discarded the error, `src/main.rs:229-233` (`Err(_) => Ok(Vec::new())`) and `src/main.rs:259` (`.unwrap_or_default()`), were CORRECT BEFORE THE WIDENING AND WRONG AFTER IT: a containment refusal became indistinguishable from "the pack ships no such file", so a run wrote a materially wrong `AGENTS.md` at exit 0 with empty stderr, byte-identical to a legitimate one. Two comments elsewhere, `src/manifest.rs:429-430` and `:485-487`, became false without being edited. THE FIX PASS'S OWN NEW TEXT WAS TRUE: the claims reviewer checked its four rewritten claim sites and found all four true, the triager re-ran three of them, and exactly one new false statement was authored by the pass, a `low`, false only on a platform this environment cannot run. So the triage's own conclusion is that a claims lens over a fix pass's new text could not have found the round's `high`, and what finds it is enumerating the CONSUMERS of any value whose domain the change widens, then running the pre-change and post-change binaries against shapes outside the existing test set. The same triage named a twin form, INPUT-SET WIDENING WITHOUT RE-ENUMERATING: the refusal's input set grew from strings a pack author writes deliberately to any file a deployment tool happens to link, and the pass disclosed the two shapes it tested and enumerated none it did not. THE DELTA AGAINST THE AUDIT: the triage states in terms that this is not the mechanism the audit named. Its own attribution shows why a constraint on what a fix pass may AUTHOR does not reach this shape. The round's `high` is a BEHAVIOUR the pass introduced, plus two pre-existing comments it invalidated without touching them, and one of the round's `low`s (`claims 2`) is that same invalidation shape on five more sites.

MECHANISM 2, THE UNMEASURED COMPARATIVE CLAIM (round 3, `306d13a`). Six of round 3's eight reviewer findings (nine valid in total, counting `Z1`, which the triager raised itself) were new prose of one grammatical shape: "X now, where before or elsewhere it was Y", with the Y half never run. The triage tabulated each with the single command that falsifies it: run the previous release's binary; run the pre-change suite under the over-tightening; run a pack with both literals linked; run `validate --workflow` with an absolute and a `..`-bearing `--metrics`; grep for a join in `plan::source`; write a swallowing caller. Not one was run. Its summary is that the pass verified what it BUILT and asserted what it REPLACED. THE SECOND-ORDER DRIVER, which that triage calls the most useful thing in its document: the false sentences trace back to the PREVIOUS ROUND'S TRIAGE remedy text, carried into the tree. `X3` is a near-verbatim carry of `v002-r2-triage.md:363`, "nothing currently pins it at any level", an assertion that triage made without running the pre-change suite. `X5` and `X6` are the two artefacts round 2's `B2` remedy asked for by name, and that remedy's pointer at `README.md:242` is what produced the false "the same rule". `X1` is the residue of round 2's `claims 3` remedy, which scoped the fix to a parenthetical and did not check the clause the parenthetical sat inside. A remedy stated as an assertion becomes a claim in the tree, and the next round falsifies the claim, so the review loop is a source of its own next round's findings. One caution for a reader of the source: that section counts these as "THREE of the six" while its own list names four sites (`X1`, `X3`, `X5`, `X6`). The four sites are the measured part.

MECHANISM 3, THE DELETION-VERSUS-AUTHORING PARTITION (round 4, `01333f3`). THIS IS THE ONE THAT CORRECTS THE AUDIT. Round 3's fix pass (`fde1d60`) was a deletion pass by instruction. The triager partitioned its edit sites by what the pass DID at each one, attributed every finding of the round to a site with `git log -S`, and confirmed each against three separately built release binaries (HEAD, the pre-fix tree, and `main` at 0.0.1), verified distinct by `md5sum`. NINE SITES:

- FOUR PURE-DELETION SITES: two `CHANGELOG.md` bullets removed with one sentence moved verbatim, `README.md:325`, `src/safe_path.rs:1-7`, and `tests/...:383-385`. ZERO findings between them.
- FIVE SITES WHERE THE PASS AUTHORED SOMETHING: `src/manifest.rs:1319-1320` (delete, then write a shorter replacement) 0 findings; `tests/...:445-469` (write a new test and its comment) 0; `src/manifest.rs:524-528` (delete, then write a replacement clause) 1; `CHANGELOG.md:37` (delete, then write a replacement bullet) 1; `src/main.rs:2110-2124` (write new code, a comment and a message) 2. FOUR findings in total.

SO EVERY FINDING OF THE ROUND SITS AT A SITE WHERE THE PASS AUTHORED SOMETHING, AND NO PURE-DELETION SITE PRODUCED ONE. The implication runs one way only: two of the five authored sites produced nothing, and one produced two, so an authored site is not a finding each. One arithmetic caution for a reader of the source: its prose says "seven edit sites" while its own table lists nine, and nine is what the table's own counts add to (4 plus 5).

THE DELETIONS THEMSELVES WORKED, measured in the same round. Every string round 3 falsified is gone, checked per string at HEAD and at `HEAD~1`, and no replacement inherited the falsity, checked replacement by replacement. Four of the five NEW comparative claims the pass authored hold, each run by the triager, so the falsification rate on newly authored comparative claims fell from 6 of 6 to 1 of 5.

THE CORRECTION TO THE AUDIT'S RECOMMENDATION 3, STATED EXPLICITLY. The audit (`docs/plans/workflow-calibration.explorations/2026-08-13-audit-when-the-loop-turned.md`, recommendation 3 and Condition 2) says to constrain what a fix pass may do, on the measurement that deletion-only and number-edit-only fixes re-seed at close to zero while fix passes that author prose re-seed at close to 100%. That framing puts the variable on the PASS. Round 4 measured it on the SITE, and the partition does not fall where the audit puts it: `fde1d60` was a deletion pass and it still produced four findings at a re-seeding rate of 80%, and TWO OF THE FOUR ARE AT SITES WHERE THE PASS DELETED AND THEN WROTE A REPLACEMENT, which the audit's framing would score on the deletion side. The operative constraint is therefore not "delete rather than rewrite". It is whether the pass AUTHORS A REPLACEMENT SENTENCE AT ALL, at any site. Both records are cited so a reader can check the correction rather than take it: the audit at the path above, and `v002-r4-triage.md` at `01333f3`, under "The correction, and what it implies for a fifth round".

WHAT THE ROUND 4 TRIAGER DREW FROM THAT MEASUREMENT, recorded as its inference and not as a measurement: every remaining edit must be a deletion, and where a claim cannot be deleted outright, its replacement must be copied verbatim from a measurement already in a findings file. Its stated reason a deletion-only rule cannot stand alone is that a pass cannot delete its way to a new error message or a new `CHANGELOG.md` bullet.

MECHANISM 4, THE SURVIVING TEXT RE-SCOPED BY WHAT WAS DELETED (round 6, `7ed86f8`). THIS IS THE FOURTH MEASUREMENT OF THIS MECHANISM AND ITS TRIAGER SAYS SO IN ITS OWN TEXT. Read this record first, ahead of the three above it, for the reason the supersession paragraph below gives. Its subject is the deletion cut the human authorised at the cap escalation. The triager extracted the 0.0.2 release section pre-cut and post-cut and tested every surviving bullet for byte-identity against its pre-cut form: 21 bullets before and 15 after, made of 7 deleted outright, 12 untouched survivors, 2 rewritten in place and 1 authored new. FINDINGS BY CLASS: the 7 whole-bullet deletions produced ZERO between them; the 2 partial-sentence edits raised 3 and produced 2 valid; the 1 authored bullet produced 1; and the 1 finding at an untouched survivor sits on a bullet byte-identical pre-cut and post-cut, so it predates the cut rather than being caused by it.

WHAT IT FALSIFIES, MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. The triager ran a per-bullet word diff on the two rewritten bullets. One deleted 66 words and added two, the other deleted 55 and added three, and ALL FIVE ADDITIONS ARE PUNCTUATION OR CAPITALISATION REPAIRS AT A CUT SEAM: a mid-sentence clause became a sentence start and took a capital, a semicolon-joined half was removed so a semicolon became a full stop, and a list lost its third item so the conjunction before the second became a comma. NOT ONE NEW CONTENT WORD WAS AUTHORED INTO EITHER BULLET, AND BOTH STILL PRODUCED FINDINGS. So the findings did not come from authored text.

THE ACTUAL MECHANISM. A partial cut silently RE-SCOPES the text that survives, because quantifiers, anaphors, definite articles and contrast structures in the surviving text were calibrated against the text that was removed. The round's own three instances: a definite plural plus a two-item apposition that still read as a complete enumeration after the count word and one list item went; an anaphor ("neither") whose antecedent pair lost a member; and an outcome description that was disambiguated by a following sentence which the cut deleted. Deleting a WHOLE unit cannot do this, because nothing inside it survives to be re-scoped.

THE CHECK THAT FOLLOWS, and it caught a live instance in the very pass that adopted it: after a partial cut, re-read the whole surviving unit and resolve every "neither", "both", "each", "the two", "these" and "it" in it against what is actually still there. A whole-unit deletion carries a different obligation, the inbound-reference sweep below.

HOW MECHANISM 4 SUPERSEDES THE THREE ABOVE, STATED EXPLICITLY BECAUSE A READER WHO APPLIES ALL FOUR GETS A CONSTRAINT THAT HAS SINCE BEEN MEASURED WRONG. The audit's recommendation 3 puts the variable on what a fix pass AUTHORS. Mechanism 3 sharpened that onto the SITE and concluded that the operative constraint is whether the pass authors a replacement sentence at all. Round 6 measured a pass that authored no content word at either rewritten site and still took a finding at each, so THE AUTHORING VARIABLE IS NOT WHAT SEPARATES THE SAFE CLASS FROM THE UNSAFE ONE. What survives is WHOLE-UNIT DELETION VERSUS ANY EDIT INSIDE A UNIT, whether that edit authors anything or not. Two things are NOT overturned and must not be read as retired: mechanism 3's site-level partition, whose measurement stands and only whose stated variable is replaced; and mechanisms 1 and 2, each of which names a different shape rather than a version of the authoring model. Apply mechanism 4. Read the other three as the history of how it was reached.

THE INBOUND-REFERENCE SWEEP, PROVED BY THE TARGETED VERIFICATION THAT FOLLOWED ROUND 6 (record 343, `e82e303`). It is recorded here rather than as a fifth mechanism because a different pass proved it and because it is the obligation a WHOLE-unit deletion carries, where mechanism 4's check is the obligation a partial cut carries.

WHAT HAPPENED. The round 6 fix deleted, as a whole sentence, the claim its triage had ruled the release section's only false statement of fact. THE SAME SENTENCE SURVIVED VERBATIM IN `README.md`, which `Cargo.toml`'s `readme` field ships inside the published crate and which crates.io renders as the crate's front page. Six rounds missed it, across 6,430 lines in the eighteen reviewer and triage files those rounds produced, because every round read the `CHANGELOG` and none searched the repository for the deleted sentence's own phrases. The verifier found it with one `grep -nE` for six distinctive phrases over three files, then confirmed it reaches users by grepping the packaged tarball. The same sweep also found the claim in the `audit` subcommand's clap doc comment in `src/main.rs`, WHICH SHIPS COMPILED INTO THE BINARY.

THE GAP WAS COVERAGE AND NOT RIGOUR, which is why further rounds of the same shape would not have closed it. THE DURABLE RULE: after deleting a sentence, grep two or three of its distinctive phrases across the whole repository rather than only the file you edited, and include whatever a package manifest ships. It is one command and it is not a reviewer's judgement call.

THE PER-ROUND RE-SEEDING RATES. Three triagers measured this, each on its own attribution, and THE DENOMINATORS DIFFER, so each is given with its own.

- ROUND 2 (`d7c9fb0`): 3 of 6 VALID FINDINGS strict, 50%, where strict means text or behaviour the fix pass INTRODUCED. 4 of 6 broad, 67%, where broad adds findings whose subject the pass did not write but did make false. Weighted by severity, the pass owned the round's only `high` and only `medium`.
- ROUND 3 (`306d13a`): 7 of 8 REVIEWER FINDINGS strict, 88%, and 7 of 8 broad. A third figure the triage added because round 2's two definitions do not cover the shape it found, "text this pass wrote OR rewrote": 8 of 8. The denominator excludes the ninth valid finding of the round, which the triager raised itself and attributed to the round 1 pass. Weighted by severity the picture inverts: seven `low`s, and no defect of any severity in the code the pass changed.
- ROUND 4 (`01333f3`): 4 of 5 strict, 80%, counting defect SITES rather than findings so the numbers compare, because one finding was merged from two reviewers and carries two halves.
- The audit's project-wide baseline, for comparison: 49% strict and 61% broad, across 189 of 211 round-2-onward findings.

Round 4 stated the series and what it shows. 50%, then 88%, then 80%: THE RATE IS FLAT WITHIN NOISE AND THE ABSOLUTE COUNT FELL, from 8 findings with 7 re-seeded to 5 findings with 4 re-seeded.

ROUND 6 IS ABSENT FROM THAT SERIES DELIBERATELY, AND ITS ABSENCE IS NOT A GAP TO FILL. Its triage partitioned the cut by SITE CLASS and did not compute a strict or broad rate, so putting it on this axis would mean deriving a figure its own measurement does not support. Its partition is under mechanism 4 above, and mechanism 4 is why the axis this series measures is the wrong one anyway.

THE CAUSATION QUESTION IS OPEN AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT ANSWERED HERE (`Q-76`, human, 2026-08-14). Capturing these mechanisms now was chosen over running the causation investigation immediately and over doing neither until the release ships. The audit established WHEN the loop turned and WHAT changed, and it did not establish WHY. The untested hypothesis, its dates, and the two reasons coincidence and reverse causation are both live are recorded in the `Q-76` item so the investigation can be picked up cold.

## The orchestrator-defect pattern, and the countermeasure that worked

CAPTURED 2026-08-14, AS ONE PATTERN AND NOT AS SEVEN ITEMS, because the pattern is the finding and the individual defects are its evidence. Like the mechanisms above, this is measurement. It adds no work item to this step.

THE PATTERN: THE ORCHESTRATOR PRODUCES CONFIDENT SUMMARIES FASTER THAN IT VERIFIES THEM, AND NOTHING IN THIS WORKFLOW CHECKS A SUMMARY BEFORE IT BECOMES A BRIEF OR A DECISION. Principle 6 (Ground decisions in evidence) is the principle it breaks, and it breaks it at the handover rather than at the gathering: a summary is what a human decides on and what a writer builds from, and this workflow runs a review loop over the artifact while running nothing at all over the account of it. The 2026-08-13 audit named this in the orchestrator's own conduct before any of the defects below happened.

THE EVIDENCE IS IN THE LEDGER, BY DEFECT NUMBER, AND IS NOT COPIED HERE. Orchestrator defects (26) to (31) are in the paragraph beginning "ORCHESTRATOR DEFECTS (26) TO (31), RECORDED TOGETHER BECAUSE THEY ARE ONE PATTERN", and defect (32) is in the paragraph beginning "ORCHESTRATOR DEFECT (32), AND IT WAS OVERTURNED BY THE WRITER I BRIEFED WITH IT". Find them by that text rather than by position. Their shapes run from citing reproductions that existed only in an agent's returned report, through briefing a fix pass from a paraphrase naming one call site where the class had two, to five relayed figures that downstream agents falsified. One of them chained a harvest copy and a `git worktree remove --force` with `;`, and when the copy failed a precondition the removal destroyed both reviewers' findings files, which is the same class as the scratch-directory rule the orchestrator hands to every agent.

DEFECT (32) IS THE ONE TO ACT ON, BECAUSE IT ARRIVED WITH A COUNTERMEASURE THAT WORKED AND THAT COSTS ONE SENTENCE. The orchestrator measured a claim about the published 0.0.1 six times, on six fixtures that all ran the same masked path, and took the wrong conclusion to the human, who decided on it. Every repetition raised its confidence and not one of them changed the masking. THE WRITER BRIEFED WITH THAT CONCLUSION OVERTURNED IT, and the remedy shrank from deleting a sentence to narrowing three words inside it. The only reason it was caught is one sentence in the brief licensing the writer to contradict the orchestrator FIRST AND PROMINENTLY, given alongside the statement that the human had already decided the other way.

THE COUNTERMEASURE, STATED AS THE THING TO ADOPT: a writer handed a conclusion must be told that the conclusion may be wrong and that a correction outranks a clean report. It is one sentence in a brief and it needs no tooling. It does not replace the roles that already catch this class from outside, since defects (24) and (26) were both caught by a planner reading the orchestrator's own reasoning. What it adds is that the agent ALREADY HOLDING THE EVIDENCE is told it may contradict the brief, instead of reading the brief as the specification to satisfy.

### `user-prompts-pointer-and-drift-coverage`: name `audit.md` in the shipped prompt list, distinguish it from the `agent-flow audit` subcommand, and widen the drift guard to the `.agents/user-prompts/` copies

THREE ITEMS, HELD AS ONE STEP RATHER THAN THREE. All three concern the `.agents/user-prompts/` family, all three are small, and all three have a deterministic oracle, so holding them together costs one review loop instead of three (Minimal by default). All three were found during the 0.0.3 release work, all three were deliberately left alone there, and none is fixed by the record you are reading.

`B` is independent of the other two and can be dropped without them. `A` and `C` are not independent of each other: `C`'s guidance half is a clause inside the sentence `A` adds, so that half costs one clause once `A` is done, and `C` taken alone would have to author `A`'s sentence first, since a list that does not name `audit.md` cannot distinguish it from anything. `C` IS NOT ONE CLAUSE IN TOTAL: it has two prose sites, one of them outside the guidance in `src/main.rs`, and it owns this step's whole `CHANGELOG.md` edit. Size it from its own section, not from this paragraph.

`A` and `C` together change what `agent-flow scaffold` emits and what `agent-flow --help` prints, so they owe a CHANGELOG entry; `B` owes none. `C` also carries a second, separately decided CHANGELOG correction, `Q-77-changelogfix`, which lands in the same new section of the same file and which this fold's own measurement of what 0.0.3 shipped found, rather than the release work. All of that is worked out and sited under `C`.

### `A`: `audit.md` is not named in the shipped getting-started prompt list

`pack/AGENTS.md` opens with a getting-started paragraph that names the human-invoked prompts by filename, and a later paragraph that names the ones carrying state across a break. Between them they name six: `kickoff.md`, `explore.md` and `review.md` in the first, `pause.md`, `compaction-prep.md` and `resume.md` in the second. Measured on the tree: `audit.md` is named zero times in `pack/AGENTS.md`, zero times in the generated root `AGENTS.md`, and zero times in `.agents/AGENTS.reference.md`, while `kickoff.md` is named in all three. So a user whose only entry point is the shipped guidance cannot discover the seventh prompt from it. The README's scaffolded-layout block does list all seven, which is why acceptance criterion 5 of `audit-user-prompt` was met while this gap stayed open.

THIS DOES NOT RE-OPEN THE SELF-CONTAINED-VERSUS-ENTRY-MODE DECISION `audit-user-prompt` settled, and the distinction is the whole reason it is safe to do. That decision was about where the audit DISCIPLINES live, and it put them in the prompt so the shipped guidance would not grow a fifth mode paragraph. What is missing here is a POINTER, one clause naming a file, which carries no discipline into the guidance and adds no mode, no role and no phase.

THE COST, STATED SO IT IS WEIGHED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. `pack/AGENTS.md` is the source of the generated guidance, so editing it widens the regeneration set to the root `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/AGENTS.reference.md`, which the drift guard's checks 1 and 2 pin. The 2026-08-13 audit's recommendation 8 wants the shipped guidance cut rather than grown; one clause against that target is negligible, and the alternative of leaving the prompt undiscoverable from the guidance is the worse trade. Name the trade in the outcome either way.

ACCEPTANCE, each executable:

1. `audit.md` is named by filename in `pack/AGENTS.md`, in the full-path form `.agents/user-prompts/audit.md`, matching the form line 7 already uses for `kickoff.md`, `explore.md` and `review.md`, not line 11's bare-filename form, which is used for the state-carrying prompts `audit.md` is not one of.
2. The root `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/AGENTS.reference.md` are regenerated in the same change, by running `cargo run -- scaffold --output-dir . --write --force --principles default --instrument`. That is the first line of the `scaffold-self` recipe in `justfile` verbatim. Do NOT run its second line, `nix fmt`, which is the repo-wide formatter that `AGENTS.md`'s "Format only your own files" rule forbids an implementer from running. `--force` is required rather than incidental, because `pack/pack.toml` declares `AGENTS.md` as `ownership = "working"` and a run without the flag leaves the file alone. `cargo test` then passes, which is what makes the drift guard's checks 1 and 2 assert the regeneration happened. MEASURED, so that skipping `nix fmt` is not taken on trust: run into an empty directory against the current tree, every file this command produces is byte-identical to its committed copy, both generated guidance files included, so after the `pack/AGENTS.md` edit the run's diff is confined to those two.
3. Nothing else in the guidance moves. No mode paragraph, no role and no phase is added.

### `B`: the `.agents/user-prompts/` copies sit outside the whole-file drift guard

PRE-EXISTING, and documented as a scope call in the module that owns it rather than discovered here. `src/agents_md_drift.rs` runs three comparisons. Checks 1 and 2 pin the committed root `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/AGENTS.reference.md` against a fresh render. Check 3 filters the rendered asset set by `PROMPT_DEST_PREFIX`, which is `.agents/prompts/`, so it covers the role prompts and nothing else. The module's COMPLEMENT rule states the consequence directly and names the `.agents/user-prompts/` copies as one of its illustrations. So nothing pins the committed `.agents/user-prompts/audit.md` against `pack/user-prompts/audit.md`, and the same holds for the other six copies: an edit to a committed copy, or a pack edit without a regeneration, ships a divergence that no gate reports.

THE MODULE HAS ALREADY PRICED THE FIX AND THE PRICE IS WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH DOING NOW. Its own rule records that widening to the Markdown asset copies is a small change to check 3's filter, because they are prose under the same prettier settings and already satisfy the `assert_no_unprotected_construct` precondition, whereas the `.toml` copies under `.agents/` would need a comparison of their own and are NOT in scope here. Widening the filter also inherits the module's accepted `R1` residual, which is that check 3 maps render to committed and asserts nothing in the other direction, so a committed copy the pinned render does not emit stays invisible to it. That residual is not this step's to close.

THE ALTERNATIVE IS TO LEAVE IT, and it is not unreasonable: the gap is documented where a maintainer meets it, and a user-prompt copy going stale ships worse guidance rather than worse behaviour. Take that option only by writing it down as a decision, because the module's rule already anticipates the widening and an undocumented no is indistinguishable from an oversight.

ACCEPTANCE, each executable:

1. Check 3 covers the `.agents/user-prompts/` copies as well as the `.agents/prompts/` ones, by widening the filter rather than by adding a hand-written list, so the check stays self-extending when the pack gains a prompt.
2. Red then green, demonstrated rather than asserted: hand-edit one committed `.agents/user-prompts/` copy, show the guard fails, revert, show it passes. The red state lands as evidence in the outcome.
3. The module doc's COVERAGE block is updated in the same change, since it currently states these copies as an illustration of what is NOT covered, and that sentence becomes false. The `.toml` copies stay out of scope and stay named as out of scope.
4. `cargo test` passes and no other guarded comparison changes.

### `C`: `audit` names two unrelated things, and neither name says which one (`Q-77`)

THE GAP, MEASURED ON THE TREE rather than asserted. `agent-flow audit` is the advisory code-value report (`src/audit.rs`, built by `code-value-audit-static`) and `.agents/user-prompts/audit.md` is the pasted prompt carrying the pre-registered measurement method (built by `audit-user-prompt`). They share no machinery, no input and no output. What each place says today: the subcommand's help text is the single-paragraph doc comment at `src/main.rs:424`, and it names the prompt zero times; `pack/AGENTS.md` contains the string `audit` zero times in any case, so the shipped guidance names neither of the two; the generated root `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/AGENTS.reference.md` contain it once each, at line 145, as the word `auditable` inside the decision-receipt schema, which is a third and unrelated sense. `README.md` names both: `audit.md` at line 49 in the scaffolded-layout block, and the subcommand at line 216 in the "Validating and projecting workflow state" section and again through the "Auditing code value" section that begins at line 270. Line 49 and that section are 221 lines apart, and nothing at line 49 points to either. So a user who reads `agent-flow --help` and then the shipped guidance has the word and nothing else, which is the gap `Q-77` records.

THE DECISION THIS IMPLEMENTS. `Q-77` (human, 2026-08-15) chose to keep both names and to distinguish them in the `audit` subcommand's help text and in the shipped prompt list, over renaming the subcommand, over renaming the prompt, and over ruling the collision acceptable in the queue alone. The queue entry carries the reasoning, what was rejected and why, and the principle that argues the other way. This item is that decision's whole implementation. It carries one further thing `Q-77` did not choose, the 0.0.3 CHANGELOG correction decided separately as `Q-77-changelogfix` and specified below, which sits here because it lands in the same new section of the same file, not because it belongs to the naming decision.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT RE-OPEN. It renames nothing, in either direction, and it does not settle whether the two names should differ; the collision stands and `Q-77` says so in as many words. It adds no mode, no role and no phase to the shipped guidance, which is the same boundary item `A` holds and for the same reason. It does not touch `pack/user-prompts/audit.md`: that prompt's opening paragraph already states what it is for, and a reader who is already inside the prompt is not choosing between it and a subcommand.

THE COST, STATED SO IT IS WEIGHED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. The guidance half is a clause inside a sentence item `A` is adding, so against `A` its marginal cost is one clause and no extra regeneration. The help half is one sentence added to a doc comment that already runs to three, in a subcommand list entry that is already the longest of the seven, so `agent-flow --help` gets longer for every user including the ones who will never paste a prompt. What that buys is priced in `Q-77`: the alternative is the user who cannot tell the two apart at all.

TWO SITES, SPECIFIED HERE SO THE IMPLEMENTER AUTHORS PROSE RATHER THAN DECIDING SCOPE.

SITE 1 IS THE HELP TEXT AT `src/main.rs:424`, the doc comment on the `Audit(AuditArgs)` variant of `enum Command`. Append one sentence to the EXISTING paragraph rather than starting a new one. MEASURED on the built binary: the current single-paragraph doc comment reaches `agent-flow --help` and `agent-flow audit --help` in full, so appending to it is known to reach `agent-flow --help`, which is the path `Q-77` names. The reason not to start a second paragraph is clap's documented derivation, the short `about` coming from the first paragraph and the `long_about` from the whole, which would put a second paragraph in `agent-flow audit --help` alone; that half is the documented rule and was NOT run here, which is why criterion 1 checks the outcome rather than the rule. The sentence states that this subcommand is unrelated to the `audit.md` user prompt, names `.agents/user-prompts/audit.md` in full so it is greppable and pasteable, and says in one clause what that prompt does. NOTHING PINS THE HELP STRINGS: no test in the repository reads any CLI help output. `grep -rn -- '--help' tests/` returns nothing, so no test asks the binary for help, and `grep -rn 'Usage' tests/` returns nothing, so none asserts on the usage text clap prints on a bad invocation either. So `cargo test` neither catches a mistake here nor objects to a correct change, which is why criterion 1 runs the built binary instead.

SITE 2 IS THE PROMPT LIST IN `pack/AGENTS.md`, inside the getting-started paragraph at line 7. That is where `A`'s pointer sentence belongs, rather than the later paragraph at line 11, because line 11 names the prompts that carry state across a break and `audit.md` does not. The distinguishing text is a subordinate clause on `A`'s pointer sentence, naming `agent-flow audit` and what it reports. It is not its own sentence and not its own paragraph, which is the boundary this item's own acceptance criterion 2 pins; `A`'s criterion 3 is the adjacent and different constraint, that no mode paragraph, role or phase is added. `pack/AGENTS.md` already names one subcommand in prose, `agent-flow render`, twice on line 30, so naming a second subcommand there introduces no new kind of reference into the shipped guidance.

THE CHANGELOG CONSEQUENCE, WORKED OUT RATHER THAN ASSUMED. `agent-flow` 0.0.3 was published on 2026-08-15, and `CHANGELOG.md` has `## [0.0.3] - 2026-08-15` as its newest section with no Unreleased section above it. Items `A` and `C` are both user-visible: after them every `scaffold` run emits different `AGENTS.md` prose, and `agent-flow --help` prints a sentence it did not print before. Item `B` is not user-visible: `src/agents_md_drift.rs` is a doc comment plus a single `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, so it compiles to nothing in a release build. So this step's own entry covers `A` and `C` together, in a new `## [Unreleased]` section inserted above `## [0.0.3] - 2026-08-15`, under a `### Changed` subheading, because both halves amend shipped text rather than adding a feature. The bare `## [Unreleased]` heading is this repository's own form, closed into a dated heading at release: `c9f2b33` closed one into `## [0.0.2] - 2026-08-13`. Two further pieces go in that same new section, specified two paragraphs below. Every piece's wording is the implementer's.

THE PRECEDENT THAT ARGUES AGAINST AN ENTRY, MEASURED AND RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT FOR A REVIEWER TO FIND. Two changes of this kind carried no entry. `faf2e2d` edited this same `audit` help text and authored no CHANGELOG clause for it, and says so in its own commit message. `a5bb7ee` added `pack/user-prompts/audit.md` and `.agents/user-prompts/audit.md` and touched `CHANGELOG.md` not at all; it is an ancestor of `v0.0.3`, so 0.0.3 shipped a whole new scaffolded prompt that the CHANGELOG never records. The entry is owed here anyway, because 0.0.3's own entry claims that "the only content change in the scaffolded assets is the command name inside their prose", and a change to scaffolded asset content that goes unrecorded makes that class of claim uncheckable for the next reader. THE `a5bb7ee` OMISSION WAS ROUTED TO THE HUMAN AND HAS BEEN RULED ON, so it IS this step's to fix, forward only. The next paragraph specifies that.

THE 0.0.3 CORRECTION, DECIDED SEPARATELY AS `Q-77-changelogfix` (human, 2026-08-15; `type:"decision"` receipt in `docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl`). WHAT IS FALSE, MEASURED. `pack/user-prompts/audit.md` and `.agents/user-prompts/audit.md` exist at `v0.0.3` and at neither path at `v0.0.2`, and they are the only files added to either directory between the two tags: `git ls-tree -r --name-only v0.0.2` filtered to those two directories returns six entries each, and the same at `v0.0.3` returns seven each, the difference being `audit.md`. `a5bb7ee` is an ancestor of `v0.0.3` and not of `v0.0.2`. So 0.0.3's own claim that "Every subcommand, flag, option, pack format and scaffolded file layout is the same as 0.0.2", at `CHANGELOG.md` line 11, is false: the scaffolded layout gained a seventh user prompt. 0.0.3 also carries no `### Added` subheading at all, so that prompt is recorded nowhere in the file.

CORRECT FORWARD ONLY, which is what the decision chose. The `## [0.0.3] - 2026-08-15` section stays exactly as published, so the repository and the immutable crates.io tarball keep saying the same thing. Both pieces go under the new `## [Unreleased]`: an `### Added` entry recording the `audit.md` user prompt that 0.0.3 shipped, and an explicit correction of 0.0.3's scaffolded-file-layout clause, naming what actually changed. REJECTED, recorded so the exception stays visible: editing the 0.0.3 section in place, which makes the repository and the tarball disagree; editing it silently, which is changed history with no note; and leaving it, which leaves a published false statement of fact standing while a correction is available. ### `sidecar-status-opening-drift`: DELETE the duplicated status label from the 21 step sidecars whose opening contradicts the step's declared `status` (`Q-78-statusdrift`, `Q-78-statusform`)

THE GOVERNING FACT, WHICH AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS STEP NEVER NAMED. `docs/plans/agent-scaffold.documentation-protocol.md:5`, rendered at `docs/plans/agent-scaffold.md:26`, ends: "The Step Details below carry each step's design, decisions, and (once done) outcome and evidence, and do not repeat the status label." An earlier draft directed the implementer to write a corrected label into all 21, which would have authored 21 fresh violations of that sentence, and it routed the question to `Q-78` as undecided when for this plan the protocol had already decided it.

THIS PROJECT HAS RULED THE DUPLICATION A DEFECT TWICE, AND THE SECOND RULING WAS WAITING FOR EXACTLY THIS STEP. `docs/plans/agent-scaffold.ledger.md:46` records round 2 finding G1, a bundle including "repeats `next` status label", and `:62` records the triager ruling it VALID at `high`. `:99` records round 3 finding L1, "`state-schema` repeats its status label", and `:101` records all eight findings of that round valid, with L1 alone left unfixed for one stated reason: "the leading status-word is a plan-wide convention, do not single out `state-schema` (leave it)". L1 WAS RAISED WHILE THE LABEL WAS ACCURATE, since `state-schema` was `deferred` and its opening said "Deferred", and it was still valid. So the DUPLICATION is the defect, independent of whether the copy currently happens to be right, and writing 21 accurate labels would not close the class. This step is the pass over the 21 mismatching openings that L1's triager deferred to, which answers its "do not single out `state-schema`" objection because `state-schema` is one of the 21. It does not close the class: 24 sidecars keep an accurate label and survive it untouched, as the residual recorded under NOT IN SCOPE below states.

ONE FILE SET, SELECTED BY A COMMAND RATHER THAN BY A READING; ONE OBLIGATION, WHICH IS A READING. A step's `status` lives in `docs/plans/agent-scaffold.plan.toml` and is the single source of truth for it. Forty-five of the 101 step sidecars ALSO open by naming a state in prose, and that second copy was never maintained: 21 of the 45 now name a state their step is not in. Those 21 files are the scope, and a command selects them so the set cannot be argued about. Inside each of the 21, the token GOES and the obligation is the whole opening LINE, which takes a reading rather than a strip, for reasons measured under WHAT THE FIX IS below. It changes nothing else about any step.

TWO HUMAN DECISIONS, WHICH DECIDE DIFFERENT THINGS, kept apart because an earlier draft conflated them. `Q-78-statusdrift` (human, 2026-08-18) decided the TIMING AND ROUTE: fix this now as its own step, over folding it into the `Q-78` design pass and over flipping the affected statuses to `not-started`. `Q-78-statusform` (human, 2026-08-18) decided the FORM: DELETE the state token from the 21 openings rather than replace it, and record the residual as a named exclusion. THE REASONING ACCEPTED, cited by name: Principle 8, Structured data first, project for humans, which names plan status first among the data that must have one structured home with the human views derived by projection, and which directs that the best long-term design beats minimal blast radius at this pre-adoption stage; and Principle 1, Prefer the cleaner long-term architecture over the smallest diff. WHAT THE CRITERIA NEVER SETTLED, MEASURED, so the ruling is not mistaken for something the step already implied. WHY NEITHER RECEIPT IS IN `[step.provenance].decisions`, RECORDED SO THE ABSENCE IS A CHOICE. `decisions` resolves fail-closed to a registered `[[question]]` id of `Q-<n>` shape: the provenance arm of `validate_source` (`src/plan/source.rs`) rejects a decision that `question_id_index` (`src/metrics.rs:427`) cannot parse, and then rejects one that names no `[[question]]`. `Q-78-statusdrift` and `Q-78-statusform` are both sub-decision ids with a receipt and no registered `[[question]]`, the same convention `Q-55-<suffix>`, `Q-65-<suffix>` and `Q-77-changelogfix` already follow, so putting either there would fail `validate --source` on both arms. ### THE DRIFT, MEASURED

THE METHOD, so the number is reproducible rather than asserted. For each of the 101 Roadmap steps, take the first line of `docs/plans/agent-scaffold.steps/<slug>.md` that is neither blank nor a Markdown heading, and read its leading word or phrase. When that leading token is one of the seven Roadmap status labels (`not started`, `in progress`, `complete`, `skipped`, `next`, `optional`, `deferred`), compare it against the step's declared `status`. Report every pair that disagrees. The 101st step is this one, whose opening carries no such token. THIS TEST SELECTS THE FILES AND DOES NOT DEFINE THE FIX: it reads the leading token only, while the obligation under WHAT THE FIX IS covers the whole opening line. Keeping the two apart is deliberate, because a selector has to be mechanical and the obligation cannot be.

TWO PAIRS DISAGREE ON THE TOKEN AND AGREE ON THE FACT, so they are exempt and the exemption is stated rather than silent. `optional` and `deferred` say nothing about whether work has started, so an opening of "Not started" alongside either adds information without contradicting it. Four sidecars are exempt on that ground: `git-url-fetch` (`deferred`, and its opening names both, "Not started (deferred)."), and `greenfield-flake`, `later-enhancements` and `tui-authoring` (all `optional`). No other pair is exempt: `complete` and `in progress` both assert that work happened, so an opening of "Not started", "Next" or "Deferred" on either contradicts the declared status outright.

THE COUNT IS 21 OF 101, MEASURED ON THE TREE THIS STEP IS AUTHORED INTO. Ten `complete` steps open "Not started": `optional-modules`, `instrument-flag`, `reviewer-harness-field`, `reviewer-diversity`, `review-mode`, `doc-redundancy-cleanup`, `doc-currency-guidance`, `human-input-gate-reinforce`, `planner-folds-decisions` and `prompt-drift-guard`. Seven `complete` steps open "Next": `session-preflight`, `round-log-core`, `workflow-invariants`, `decision-receipt`, `structured-skeleton`, `reviewer-reproducible-evidence` and `decision-folder-currency`. Two `complete` steps open "Deferred": `state-schema` and `checks-runner-worktree-name-collision`. Two of the three `in-progress` steps open "Not started": `workflow-calibration` and `workflow-driver`.

THE THIRD `in-progress` STEP IS CLEAN AND IS NAMED SO THE READER KNOWS IT WAS CHECKED. `code-value-audit-static` opens "Build the Tier-0 slice of the Q-52 code-value audit", which is a statement of what the step does and not a claim about its state, so it contradicts nothing. Of the 80 sidecars this step does not touch, 56 open with no status token at all (this one included), 20 open with a token that matches the declared status, and 4 are the exempt pairs named above. 56 plus 20 plus 4 plus 21 is 101.

### WHY THE STATUS IS RIGHT AND THE PROSE IS STALE, FOR THE TWO IN-PROGRESS CASES

This step corrects the PROSE, so the direction has to be established rather than assumed. It is established independently for each of the two, and neither derivation depends on the other.

`workflow-calibration` CONTRADICTS ITSELF INSIDE ONE FILE, which is the strongest form the evidence takes here and needs no external comparison. It opens "Not started (deferred)." and three paragraphs later states "WHERE THIS STEP'S AUDIT RECORDS LIVE (`Q-73`, human, 2026-08-13, already executed at `572e331`)", describing the 2026-08-13 audit as this step's delivered work. Outside the file: `docs/plans/workflow-calibration.explorations/` holds 12 files, and `docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl` carries two `type:"decision"` receipts whose `task` is `workflow-calibration`, `Q-73` (2026-08-13) and `Q-76-causation` (2026-08-14). `workflow-driver` IS STALE ON TWO INDEPENDENTLY CHECKABLE COUNTS IN ONE SENTENCE. It opens "Not started; the build-start is a separate pending human decision, so this umbrella step stays `not-started` with no increments declared yet". First, the step declares THREE increments in the plan TOML, `workflow-driver-stage0a`, `workflow-driver-stage0b` and `workflow-driver-stage1`, so "no increments declared yet" is false against the same document the sentence sits beside. Second, `docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl` carries nine `type:"round"` records whose `task` is `workflow-driver`, spread across those three increments and dated 2026-07-19 and 07-20, plus three `type:"decision"` receipts (`Q-51` once, `Q-58` twice), and `docs/plans/workflow-driver-stage1.build-plan.md` and `docs/plans/mealy-workflow-driver.explorations/` both exist. THE OTHER 19 NEED NO SUCH DERIVATION, because they are `complete` steps and a `complete` step is by definition not "Not started", "Next" or "Deferred". One of them is close to self-correcting already and is called out so the implementer does not read it as a rewrite: `structured-skeleton` opens "Next; the planning pass is DONE (2026-07-18) and this umbrella step is built in six reviewed increments", so the same sentence that carries the stale token already says the step is built. It still gets the token fix, because a reader scanning openings reads the token.

### WHAT THE FIX IS, AND WHAT IT IS NOT

"THE OPENING" MEANS THE WHOLE OPENING LINE, AND THAT IS THE UNIT EVERYWHERE IN THIS STEP. These sidecars are not hard-wrapped, so the opening line IS the opening paragraph; measured, all 21 openings are exactly one line. Criterion 1 already reads the first non-blank, non-heading LINE, and criterion 4 bounds the diff per LINE, so the line is the unit the method and the criteria already use, and it is the unit the obligation below uses too. An earlier draft of this paragraph scoped the obligation to the opening SENTENCE while directing an edit inside `instrument-flag`'s SECOND sentence, which is the inconsistency this paragraph exists to remove.

THE FIX IS A DELETION, NOT A SUBSTITUTION (`Q-78-statusform`). The leading status token GOES and no corrected label replaces it, because the protocol sentence quoted at the top says a Step Detail does not repeat the status label, and the Roadmap table `render` generates from `[[step]].status` already carries it for every step.

THE OBLIGATION IS SEMANTIC, NOT LEXICAL. After the fix, the opening line of each of the 21 files must contain no claim that the step's declared `status` contradicts, and must read as correct prose. Deleting the leading status token is necessary and is nowhere near sufficient on either count, which is DEMONSTRATED rather than argued below.

A PLAIN STRIP IS NOT THE FIX, MEASURED. Applying a bare token deletion to all 21 in a throwaway copy leaves seven openings that do not begin as prose: `state-schema` becomes "and non-blocking (`Q-11`); ...", `workflow-calibration` becomes "(deferred). The scaffolded workflow's ...", `instrument-flag` becomes "optional. The design is decided below ...", `reviewer-reproducible-evidence` becomes "(built first, before resuming the paused ...)", and `optional-modules`, `structured-skeleton` and `workflow-driver` each begin mid-sentence in lower case. Criterion 11 is the oracle for this and it flags exactly those seven today. Each needs an AUTHORED opening, not a strip. The other 14 strip cleanly, 13 of them to "Decided (...", "Scheduled by the human ..." or "This is a/an ...", and `decision-receipt` to "The first `Q-44` structured-data pilot ...".

THE DEMONSTRATION, run on a throwaway copy of `docs/` and reproducible. Take three of the 21 and replace ONLY the leading token, leaving the rest of the line: `workflow-driver` "Not started;" to "In progress;", `optional-modules` "Not started;" to "Complete;", `workflow-calibration` "Not started (deferred)." to "In progress.". Criterion 1 then prints 18 rows instead of 21, so it certifies all three as clean while they read:

- "In progress; the build-start is a separate pending human decision, so this umbrella step stays `not-started` with no increments declared yet".
- "Complete; a design-questions pass is needed before implementing (as with `git-url-fetch`)".
- "In progress. ... This is deliberately deferred: ... so nothing here blocks earlier work".

WORKED EXAMPLES, MEASURED, AND THIS LIST IS A FLOOR RATHER THAN A SET. Each is a claim in the opening line that the declared `status` contradicts. NOTHING HERE CLAIMS THEY ARE THE ONLY ONES, and an earlier draft of this paragraph did claim exactly that, named two, and was wrong; a later count of five was also short. The implementer reads each of the 21 opening lines whole and disposes of what it finds, using criterion 9 as the starting list.

- `workflow-driver`: "so this umbrella step stays `not-started` with no increments declared yet". False twice over on an `in-progress` step that declares three increments.
- `workflow-calibration`: "This is deliberately deferred: ... so nothing here blocks earlier work". Same class as the front-matter contradiction excluded below, inside the very line being edited.
- `optional-modules`: "a design-questions pass is needed before implementing". False on a `complete` step.
- `instrument-flag`: "The design is decided below; the build is deferred". The build is not deferred on a `complete` step.
- `decision-folder-currency`: "FOUR passages are still out of step with the rule, three of them in `pack/prompts/orchestrator.md` and one in `pack/AGENTS.md`". Measured at HEAD, all four now name the planner: `pack/prompts/orchestrator.md:27` ("which is the planner's job and which you route to it rather than author yourself"), `:31` ("you route to the planner to author rather than editing the plan yourself"), `:33` ("and the planner authors that fold when it is non-trivial") and `pack/AGENTS.md:63` (the same clause). `decision-folder-currency` is the step that fixed them, and it is `complete`, so "are still out of step" is false of the tree its own sidecar sits in.
- `planner-folds-decisions`, WHICH IS ALSO CRITERION 10'S WITNESS. Its opening asserts that AGENTS.md names the planner as decision-folder only on the request-interrupt path, that the human-input-contract paragraph uses actor-less passive voice, and that the Socratic-mode paragraph only says the mode reuses the intake and Open-Questions machinery. The step's own title is "name the PLANNER as the folder of every non-trivial decided decision at the human-input-contract / Socratic-mode / checkpoint points", so its `complete` status falsifies its own opening.

ONE THING THAT IS DRIFT BUT IS NOT THIS CLASS, so it is not treated as though it were. `instrument-flag` opens "Not started; optional.", and deleting only the leading token leaves a bare "optional." fragment. It is not a self-contradiction under this step's own semantics, since the exemption argument above turns on `optional` saying nothing about whether work started, so a complete step can be an optional one. It is still drift, because `optional` is a `status` value the TOML does not carry for that step, and it is a second label to delete rather than a contradiction to resolve.

THREE BORDERLINE CASES, RULED HERE SO THE IMPLEMENTER DOES NOT HAVE TO GUESS, now that the fix is a deletion.

- `state-schema` opens with the compound "Deferred and non-blocking (`Q-11`);", so the token cannot be lifted out on its own. Author an opening that keeps the non-blocking fact and the sequencing if they are still true, and states no status at all.

Its borderline half is its closing "The human's call (2026-07-28) was to TRACK it here rather than schedule it now", which is a dated record of a past decision and stays as history.

NOT IN SCOPE, EACH CONSIDERED AND EXCLUDED SO THE ABSENCE IS A CHOICE.

- WHAT ANY OF THESE 21 STEPS SHOULD SAY. This step corrects a stale claim about state. It does not review, re-scope, re-title or rewrite a single step, and it changes no step's `status`, which is the orchestrator's.

So 45 carry a label and 24 of those (the 20 matching plus the 4 exempt) sit OUTSIDE this step's 21 and survive it untouched. ### `B`: the one non-opening sentence, in `workflow-calibration.md`

`workflow-calibration.md` also states "The directory currently holds `2026-08-13-audit-when-the-loop-turned.md` (the verdict, its evidence, and ten ordered recommendations), `2026-08-13-audit-measurement-methods.md` (the methods reference), and `calibration-analysis.md` (the 2026-07-31 prior analysis, which the audit re-tests with 12 more days of data and corrects in one place)." That reads as an exhaustive list and it names 3 of the 12 files now in `docs/plans/workflow-calibration.explorations/`. The nine it does not name are `2026-08-14-causation-investigation.md`, `finding-provenance-a.tsv`, `finding-provenance-b.tsv`, `finding-provenance-extract-a.md`, `finding-provenance-extract-b.md`, `fix-pass-shape-a.tsv`, `fix-pass-shape-b.tsv`, `fix-pass-shape-mechanical-a.md` and `fix-pass-shape-mechanical-b.md`.

WHY IT IS IN SCOPE, AGAINST THE HABIT THAT ARGUES OTHERWISE. The 2026-08-13 audit measured steps generated by the process itself rising from 8.3% to 54.2%, so "while you are in the file anyway" is the exact habit that produced that number, and it is the reason this is argued rather than assumed. It survives the test on three grounds: it is the same defect class this step is defined by, a stale statement about this step's own state; it is in the same file and two paragraphs from the opening the implementer is already editing; and it is one sentence. It does not open the door to a general currency sweep, which the exclusion above rules out explicitly.

THE IMPLEMENTER PICKS THE FORM. Either name all 12, or drop the enumeration and say what the directory is for. Naming 12 files re-creates a list that goes stale on the next write, so dropping the enumeration is the form that does not need maintaining, and the choice is left open because either satisfies the criterion.

### ACCEPTANCE, each executable

1. THE ENUMERATION IS EMPTY. Run this from the repository root and it prints nothing. It is the same command that produced the 21 above, it drives off the generated Roadmap table so it needs no JSON tool, and it encodes the `optional`/`deferred` exemption stated above.

```
sed -n 's/^| `\([a-z0-9-]*\)` | \([a-z ]*\) |.*/\1\t\2/p' docs/plans/agent-scaffold.md |
while IFS=$(printf '\t') read -r slug status; do
  line=$(sed -e '/^#/d' -e '/^[[:space:]]*$/d' "docs/plans/agent-scaffold.steps/$slug.md" | head -1)
  token=$(printf '%s' "$line" | sed -n 's/^\(Not started\|In progress\|Complete\|Skipped\|Next\|Optional\|Deferred\)\([.;,: ].*\)*$/\1/p' | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')
  case "$status:$token" in
    "$status:"|"$status:$status"|"optional:not started"|"deferred:not started") ;;
    *) printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$slug" "$status" "$token" ;;
  esac
done
```

The empty output is the oracle for the LEADING TOKEN, not the pipeline's exit status, and it is a bash snippet, so run it through the project's bash prefix rather than in nu; it uses no process substitution. MEASURED before the fix, it parses all 101 Roadmap rows and prints exactly the 21 rows listed above, so it detects the condition rather than merely staying silent. A DELETION SATISFIES IT BY CONSTRUCTION, since a line with no leading status token cannot print a mismatched one, which is why this criterion cannot be the evidence that the deletion was done well; criteria 9, 10 and 11 carry that.

CRITERION 1 IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT, WHICH IS MEASURED. On the three-file demonstration above it prints 18 rows while all three of those lines contradict themselves. Criterion 9 is what covers the rest of the line, and on that same fixture it still flags all three. Do not read an empty criterion 1 as the step being done.

2. RED THEN GREEN, demonstrated rather than asserted. Revert one corrected opening to its stale token, show criterion 1 prints that one row, restore it, show criterion 1 prints nothing again. The red output lands as evidence in the outcome.

3. EXACTLY 21 SIDECARS CHANGE, plus `docs/plans/agent-scaffold.md`. `git diff --name-only` over the step's change lists 22 paths: the 21 files under `docs/plans/agent-scaffold.steps/` named above, and the regenerated `docs/plans/agent-scaffold.md`. No file under `src/`, `pack/` or `tests/` appears, `docs/plans/agent-scaffold.plan.toml` does not appear (no `status` is flipped, and the step's own entry is authored by this planning pass rather than by the implementation), and `docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl` does not appear.

4. THE CHANGE IS CONFINED TO THE OPENING LINE, WITH ONE NAMED EXCEPTION, AND ADDS NO PARAGRAPH. For each of the 21 files, `git diff --numstat` reports at most 2 added and 2 removed lines, since each opening is one line in an unwrapped file and the fix rewrites that line in place rather than splitting it. The exception is `docs/plans/agent-scaffold.steps/workflow-calibration.md`, which carries item `B` as well and so reports at most 4 and 4.

5. ITEM `B` MAKES NO FALSE CLAIM. In `workflow-calibration.md`, every `.md` or `.tsv` filename the audit-records paragraph names exists in `docs/plans/workflow-calibration.explorations/`, and the paragraph either names all 12 entries of that directory or makes no exhaustive claim about its contents (no "the directory currently holds X, Y and Z" form).

6. THE PROJECTION IS REGENERATED AND MATCHES. `./target/debug/agent-flow render docs/plans/agent-scaffold.plan.toml` then `./target/debug/agent-flow render --check --strict docs/plans/agent-scaffold.plan.toml` exits 0, so the committed `docs/plans/agent-scaffold.md` carries the corrected Step Details. `docs/plans/agent-scaffold.md` is never hand-edited.

7. THE VALIDATORS AND THE SUITE STAY GREEN. `./target/debug/agent-flow validate --source docs/plans/agent-scaffold.plan.toml --metrics docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl` and `./target/debug/agent-flow validate --source docs/plans/agent-scaffold.plan.toml --workflow` both exit 0, and `cargo test` passes. None of the three reads sidecar prose, so they are the no-regression check rather than the oracle for this step. Criterion 1 is the oracle.

8. ASCII ONLY. `LC_ALL=C grep -cP '[^\t\x20-\x7e]' <file>` prints 0 for every changed file. Use that pattern rather than `[^ -~]`, which matches every hard tab. Note `grep -c` exits 1 when the count is 0, so it breaks an `&&` chain.

9. EVERY ROW OF THE DISPOSITION LIST IS DISPOSED OF. This is NOT a pass-or-fail oracle and its empty output is not the target; a whole-line keyword scan cannot be one, because several matches are legitimate prose (`reviewer-harness-field` describes an "OPTIONAL `harness` string", `workflow-invariants` records that the `ledger-parse` keystone was SKIPPED). It is a bounded worklist over the same 21 files, carrying the slugs literally so it keeps working after criterion 1 goes empty. Run it under bash; it uses no process substitution.

```
sed -n 's/^| `\([a-z0-9-]*\)` | \([a-z ]*\) |.*/\1\t\2/p' docs/plans/agent-scaffold.md |
while IFS=$(printf '\t') read -r slug status; do
  case " state-schema optional-modules workflow-calibration instrument-flag session-preflight round-log-core workflow-invariants decision-receipt structured-skeleton reviewer-harness-field reviewer-diversity review-mode workflow-driver doc-redundancy-cleanup doc-currency-guidance human-input-gate-reinforce reviewer-reproducible-evidence planner-folds-decisions decision-folder-currency prompt-drift-guard checks-runner-worktree-name-collision " in
    *" $slug "*) ;;
    *) continue ;;
  esac
  line=$(sed -e '/^#/d' -e '/^[[:space:]]*$/d' "docs/plans/agent-scaffold.steps/$slug.md" | head -1)
  hits=$(printf '%s' "$line" |
    grep -o -i -E 'not started|not-started|in progress|in-progress|complete|skipped|next|optional|deferred|to be done|still|pending|not yet|before implementing' |
    tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | sed 's/-/ /' | sort -u |
    grep -v -x "$status" | tr '\n' ' ')
  [ -n "$hits" ] && printf '%s\t[%s]\t%s\n' "$slug" "$status" "$hits"
done
```

MEASURED before the fix, it prints 21 rows, one per file, because each still carries its own stale leading token. THE OBLIGATION: the outcome records, for every row this prints after the fix, either the correction made or the reason that match is legitimate prose. A row left with neither is the step not finished. The scan is a FLOOR and not a census: `planner-folds-decisions`' false clauses carry no status-adjacent vocabulary, because they are present-tense assertions about the wording of another file, so once its leading token is corrected this command stops flagging it while every one of those clauses is still false. That is why criterion 10 exists.

10. EVERY OPENING LINE WAS READ WHOLE. The outcome states, for each of the 21 files, that its opening line was read end to end against the step's declared `status`, and records what that reading found beyond what criterion 9 flagged. This is the criterion that is a judgement rather than a command, and it is here because the measured evidence says no command covers the class: the demonstration under criterion 1 shows a token-only fix passing, and `planner-folds-decisions` goes silent under criterion 9 once its leading token is corrected while every assertion the bullet above records is still false. That silence survives an enlarged word list: adding `remains`, `awaiting`, `planned`, `to do`, `not done`, `when built`, `blocked`, `paused`, `will be` and `yet to` picks up `doc-redundancy-cleanup` (on `when built`) and `reviewer-reproducible-evidence` (on `paused`) and still does not reach it.

11. NO OPENING IS LEFT UNGRAMMATICAL BY THE DELETION, AND NO OPENING STATES A STATUS. Run this from the repository root under bash; it prints nothing when every one of the 21 opening lines begins as prose. MEASURED on a throwaway copy given a bare token deletion, it prints exactly the seven named under WHAT THE FIX IS, so it detects the condition rather than merely staying silent.

```
for slug in state-schema optional-modules workflow-calibration instrument-flag \
  session-preflight round-log-core workflow-invariants decision-receipt \
  structured-skeleton reviewer-harness-field reviewer-diversity review-mode \
  workflow-driver doc-redundancy-cleanup doc-currency-guidance \
  human-input-gate-reinforce reviewer-reproducible-evidence \
  planner-folds-decisions decision-folder-currency prompt-drift-guard \
  checks-runner-worktree-name-collision; do
  line=$(sed -e '/^#/d' -e '/^[[:space:]]*$/d' "docs/plans/agent-scaffold.steps/$slug.md" | head -1)
  case "$line" in
    [A-Z]*|'`'*) ;;
    *) printf '%s\t%s\n' "$slug" "$(printf '%s' "$line" | cut -c1-46)" ;;
  esac
done
```

CRITERION 11 IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT FOR THE FIRST HALF OF ITS OWN HEADER, WHICH IS MEASURED. The command tests one thing, whether the opening's first character is an uppercase letter or a backtick. On the bare-strip fixture, capitalising the first character of `state-schema`'s opening and changing nothing else takes it out of this criterion's output while it reads "And non-blocking (`Q-11`); sequenced after the human-interface work", which is a fragment. Criterion 1 stays silent on it, and criterion 9 flags it only on "before implementing", which is legitimate prose in that sentence, so an implementer meeting criterion 9's obligation records it as legitimate and moves on. Do not read an empty criterion 11 as certifying the openings. The semantic bar is the one under THE OBLIGATION IS SEMANTIC above, and criterion 10's reading is what carries it. The second half of this header is a reading, not a command: no opening line of the 21 names a Roadmap status for its own step at all, which is what `docs/plans/agent-scaffold.md:26` requires and what criterion 1's empty output cannot show.

### DOCUMENTATION IMPACT

None outside `docs/plans/`. `grep -rn 'sidecar' pack/ README.md` returns matches, and they were read rather than counted: they describe the skeleton-plus-sidecar structure, the render path, and the `<task>.steps/<slug>.md` naming convention. The one that comes closest to prescribing a sidecar's content is the scaffolded template `pack/plan-template.steps/example-step.md` and its rendered copy `docs/plans/TEMPLATE.steps/example-step.md`, one heading plus "What this step does and how; once done, the outcome and the evidence." It asks for what the step does and how, not for a state, so the deletion agrees with it and no shipped guidance, prompt or template goes stale. The pack is untouched.

`docs/plans/agent-scaffold.documentation-protocol.md` is NOT edited either. This step brings 21 files into line with the sentence that file already carries; it does not change the sentence, and it does not make it true, as the 24-sidecar exclusion above records. If the `Q-78` pass rules that a sidecar never restates a TOML field for every project rather than only for this plan, `pack/plan-template.documentation-protocol.md` is where that rule would be written, and that is the pass's to schedule rather than this step's.

## Success Criteria

- One command, run from any working directory and targeting any `--output-dir`, drops the minimal core (a usable `AGENTS.md`, a planning-document template, and the core prompts) into both an empty directory and an existing repository. Writes are off unless confirmed: a run previews the plan and only writes with `--write` or the selector's Save confirmation (`--dry-run` previews explicitly), so nothing is written by accident.
- By default it creates only absent files and never modifies existing ones; `--force` is required to overwrite; a default re-run therefore reverts nothing.
- The user can choose which principles and modules to include, interactively with sane defaults or non-interactively via flags or config.
- The dropped assets are immediately usable to run one pass of the workflow (plan -> review -> implement -> review) without further setup.
- Optional modules can be added without touching or complicating the core.
- The tool can scaffold from a user-supplied template pack, not only the built-in one.
- The scaffolded workflow is internally consistent: `pack/AGENTS.md`, the prompts under `pack/prompts/`, the README diagram, and this plan state the same rules the same way, and the convergence accounting (round outcomes and the single escalation cap) is deterministic and computable from the review ledger alone.
- The self-scaffolded copies stay reliably in sync with the pack: editing a `pack/` file and running a plain `cargo build` (no manual `cargo clean`) re-embeds the change, so `scaffold-self` and the golden sync-test regenerate from the current pack, not a stale embedded one.
- The human-interface layer is present: onboarding (a "Getting started, for the human" section that points to the editable kickoff prompt in `.agents/user-prompts/` and states the human's ongoing decision duty) and a single living human-decision queue that the orchestrator updates and pushes to the human at every checkpoint.
- The scaffolded workflow carries the human-input contract (every human-input point, escalation, intake, open questions, and clarifying questions, presents options, trade-offs, a recommendation, and reasoning judged against the project's numbered Principles, scaled to stakes) and the always-separate triager rule (the triager is a separate agent, independent of both the producer and the orchestrator, for every review round).
- The scaffolded workflow carries a git-durability-and-recovery discipline: a clean tree before spawning a writer, commit-before-delete for workflow-managed files, own-files-only formatting (no repo-wide formatters or cross-owner `git checkout`), an orchestrator recovery protocol on any kill or interrupt, and destructive validation in scratch. Every spawned agent (the writers and the read-only reviewers, triager, and explorers) runs under capability-tiered isolation (container if available, else worktree, else that discipline), and the orchestrator integrates their outputs onto main.
- Review findings flow through per-agent files that other agents read directly and the ledger references by path, so no finding is lost to orchestrator transcription; the files are committed before the orchestrator deletes them.
- A compaction-prep checkpoint keeps the plan and ledger authoritative for resuming after context loss: before a compaction the orchestrator flushes and commits the plan, the ledger, and the Open-Questions queue and verifies the plan's resume anchor, and on resume state is reconstructed from `AGENTS.md`, the plan, and the ledger.
- Human-invoked user prompts (the kickoff prompt and the compaction-prep prompt) live in their own `.agents/user-prompts/` directory, separate from the role prompts in `.agents/prompts/`, and stay thin triggers that do not duplicate workflow content.
- The workflow offers a human-invokable review entry mode (a fourth entry alongside implement, explore, and question-driven input): a human can review the whole tree or a diff against a named plan's Success Criteria, ad-hoc constraints, or open-ended correctness/quality, and get a committed findings report with a handoff into an implement task, reusing the same reviewers, separate triager, severity scale, and high/critical dismissal recheck as the other review phases.
- Optional verification modules compose on the core without complicating it: a deterministic-checks module (a user-configurable, pluggable lint/format/test/mutation gate over the code, with a read-only checks-reviewer, a `{{modules}}` guidance slot that is empty and byte-identical when no module is enabled, and an optional pre-commit hook), a test-driven module (a separate test-author role and a test-first two-gate profile) that hard-depends on it, and a mutation module that hard-depends on that.
- The scaffolded workflow's reviewer/triager diversity rule spans different models OR harnesses where available, so a user running multiple CLIs is guided to spread reviewers across them to reduce shared blind spots.
- The plan's live skeleton is a structured single source of truth: a `<task>.plan.toml` holds the Roadmap (step status, order, dependencies), the Open-Questions queue (id, status, one-line ask, a `receipt` pointer to the JSONL decision record, typed `folded_into`/`superseded_by` cross-references; the queue's `options`/`chosen` stay in the JSONL decision receipt, not the TOML), the numbered Project Principles, the step<->increment links, and (per Q-46) the exemption waivers nested on their step and the W4 baseline in `[meta]`; the append-only `docs/metrics/workflow.jsonl` holds only genuine events (rounds, escalations, decisions, intakes, dismissals). Typed cross-references replace the parametric status strings, so a `decided` question and a `blocked_by` step are structured fields, not prose conventions, and `validate --source` checks each resolves.
- `agent-flow render` generates a committed-but-never-hand-edited `<task>.md` from the TOML skeleton plus opaque Markdown prose sidecars, splicing each sidecar verbatim and never parsing prose back into structure, so there is no prose round-trip and nothing to clobber: render writes only the derived `<task>.md`, and a schema violation, an unresolved cross-reference, or a missing sidecar exits non-zero and writes nothing. A do-not-edit banner heads the generated file and names its real sources, and the derived Status line and the status vocabulary are generated (not hand-maintained), so they cannot drift.
- A `render --check` guard re-renders and compares against the committed `<task>.md`, catching both a hand-edit of the generated file and a stale render after a source edit; it warns locally so a forgotten re-render never blocks an in-flight workflow step, and fails hard in CI and in the pre-commit hook so a stale plan cannot land.
- Enforcement is preserved over the migrated data as a parser swap, not a rewrite: W3, W4, W5, and the pause.md catch keep working, reading `Step`/`Question`/waiver shapes and the baseline from the TOML and the escalation evidence from the JSONL, with per-increment convergence intact, the two evidence tiers un-launderable, and W5's record-backed join to a decision-scoped escalation preserved across the two substrates.
- New `round` and `escalation` records carry a structured step/increment id, and W3 and W5 join on it in preference to the lexical `leading_slug` strip for post-migration records, so the over-strip fragility (SE-10/B6) no longer applies to newly logged increments, while pre-migration records continue to join via the leading-slug shim.
- Migrating this repo is safe and reversible: the skeleton and sidecars are built additively while the hand-authored `.md` stays the live source (`[meta].primary = "markdown"`), validated synthetic-pilot-first, shadow-rendered and fidelity-diffed against the current plan, then cut over in a single `git revert`-able commit that sets `primary = "toml"`, renders, and (per Q-46) moves and prunes the historical JSONL waiver/baseline lines; `validate` stays green at every stage, and reverting the cutover restores both the hand-authored `.md` and the pruned JSONL lines.
- The scaffolded default stays coherent: a fresh `agent-flow` run drops a `<task>.plan.toml` skeleton, starter prose sidecar directories, and a rendered `<task>.md` that are internally consistent and `validate`-green, with no `w4_baseline` (so every decision the fresh project makes requires a receipt).
- The shipped pack's prompts and docs describe the same TOML+render+sidecar plan flow the tool actually implements: a freshly scaffolded project's `pack/prompts/*` and `pack/user-prompts/kickoff.md` describe authoring and editing the `.plan.toml` skeleton plus prose sidecars, rendering the generated `<task>.md`, never hand-editing it, and `render --check`ing before commit, with no residual Markdown-only-plan authoring instructions or stale `docs/plans/TEMPLATE.md` references; and the shipped `README.md`, `pack/AGENTS.md`, and `pack/instrument.md` are current with the render architecture (the README documents `render`/`render --check` and `validate --source`, and `instrument.md` documents that every metrics record, the `type:"decision"` receipt included, carries the required `task` field via its preamble).
- The workflow's control constants (the risk-class -> required-clean-streak map, the total-round cap, the backstop severity, the phase/tier orderings, the path templates) are single-sourced in `.agents/workflow.toml`, read by both `validate --workflow` and the driver from one `WorkflowSpec`, so the enforcement checker and the driver cannot disagree about the bar and there is no code/prose duplication (a built-in default equal to today's constants, pinned by assertion, keeps an un-migrated project byte-for-byte unchanged).
- The AGENTS.md control-constant fragment is generated from the same spec via a pack render slot and byte-guarded, so the prose statement of every control constant is derived from the spec the driver executes and the two cannot drift, while the rationale prose stays hand-authored around the slot.
- An advisory, read-only `agent-flow next` reports the current per-unit state, the valid transitions, and the next action as a filled instruction prompt (role prompt + artifact + diff range + findings/ledger paths + Principle reminders), in JSON and human text, recomputed statelessly from the plan + log + ledger + spec each call, and its forward projection of the convergence arithmetic matches `validate --workflow`'s backward computation on the same files.
- The driver is non-blocking in-loop (skipping the tool never deadlocks the workflow), consumes agent/human judgment only as typed inputs and never manufactures a verdict, and hard enforcement exists only via an opt-in boundary gate (`validate --workflow --strict` in CI or a pre-commit hook) at the landing boundary rather than per-step.
- Each canonical rule and constant lives once in `pack/AGENTS.md` and the pack prompts/docs point to it rather than restating it: the type-A copies the audit found (the total-round cap value, the clean-round counts and risk-class definition, the findings-file filename templates, the four-level severity scale and its absolute-rating gloss, and the isolation tier order) are replaced by references, the type-B role-scoped procedure prose is kept, and the two type-C accuracy bugs (the README W3-absolute waiver omission and the treefmt-v2 caveat's missing single owner) are fixed.
- Documentation currency is a core cross-cutting part of the workflow: the planner assesses which docs and prompts a folded change makes stale (stated in the planner duties and `pack/AGENTS.md` phase 2), the implementer updates them, the reviewer verifies, and acceptance carries a doc-currency check that a shipped change leaves no doc or prompt stale, with no new role or optional module added.
- The workflow performs a light, stakes-scaled task-entry re-grounding before starting a step and on resume: the orchestrator writes a brief (what the task is, why it exists, the cited durable evidence including the decision receipt, and what it is about to do) sourced only from the durable artifacts (never conversation history) and pushes it for a go/no-go via the human-input contract; and a step carries structured provenance links to the decisions, findings, and commits that justify it, which `render` presents as why the step exists.
